cirebon.s: Cirebon is a port city on the north coast of Java, Indonesia, on the border between Javanese and Sundanese lands. It became the seat of a Muslim sultanate in the 15th and 16th centuries under Sunan Gunung Jati, one of the Wali Songo, and was later divided between the courts of…

carlsbad-decrees.s: The Carlsbad Decrees were measures agreed by German states at Carlsbad in August 1819 at the urging of Metternich and adopted by the Federal Diet of the German Confederation in September. Prompted by the murder of the writer August von Kotzebue by a student, they banned the…

carl-peters.s: Carl Peters was a German colonial explorer and the founder of the German East Africa Company. In 1884 he made treaties with chiefs inland from the Zanzibar coast, which Germany placed under imperial protection in 1885.

curt-von-francois.s: Curt von François was a German army officer and explorer in Africa. As commander of the protectorate troops in South West Africa, he founded Windhoek in 1890 as the colony's military and administrative centre.

charminar.s: The Charminar is a monument and mosque in the centre of Hyderabad, India, built in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of the Golconda Sultanate when he founded the city. Its square body is crowned at each corner by a minaret about 56 metres high, which gives the building its…

convention-peoples-party.s: The Convention People's Party is a Ghanaian political party founded by Kwame Nkrumah in June 1949 after he broke with the United Gold Coast Convention. Demanding 'self-government now', it won the elections of 1951, 1954 and 1956, led the Gold Coast to independence as Ghana in…

caravaggio.s: Caravaggio, born Michelangelo Merisi, was an Italian painter whose dramatic realism and strong contrasts of light and shadow transformed European painting around 1600. Working in Rome from the 1590s, he painted works such as The Calling of Saint Matthew.

corrientes.s: Corrientes is a city in north-eastern Argentina on the east bank of the Paraná river and the capital of Corrientes Province. Founded in 1588 by Juan Torres de Vera y Aragón, it was a river port of the Spanish Río de la Plata colonies and, after independence, the centre of a…

calchaqui-wars.s: The Calchaquí Wars were a series of risings by the Diaguita peoples of the Calchaquí valleys in north-western Argentina against Spanish rule between 1560 and 1667. The largest, in 1630–1643 and 1658–1659, the latter led by the adventurer Pedro Bohórquez, who claimed Inca…

coca-spain.s: Coca is a town in the province of Segovia, Spain, the ancient Cauca of the Vaccaei. In 151 BCE the Roman general Lucullus massacred its inhabitants after they had surrendered.

congress-of-cucuta.s: The Congress of Cúcuta was the constituent assembly of Gran Colombia, meeting at Villa del Rosario de Cúcuta from May to October 1821. It joined Venezuela and New Granada in a centralised republic, adopted the Constitution of 1821, elected Simón Bolívar president and Francisco…

convention-of-ocana.s: The Convention of Ocaña was a constitutional assembly of Gran Colombia that met at Ocaña in New Granada from April to June 1828 to reform the Constitution of 1821. Bolívar's supporters, who wanted a stronger central government, and the followers of Santander, who favoured…

charlotte-grand-duchess-of-luxembourg.s: Charlotte was Grand Duchess of Luxembourg from 1919 to 1964, succeeding her sister Marie-Adélaïde, who abdicated after being accused of pro-German conduct. A referendum in 1919 confirmed the monarchy under her.

cosimo-ii-de-medici.s: Cosimo II de' Medici was Grand Duke of Tuscany from 1609 to 1621. He supported trade at Livorno and his galleys fought Ottoman and Barbary corsairs, but he is best remembered as Galileo's patron: Galileo named the moons of Jupiter the 'Medicean stars' in his honour in 1610,…

chol-khan.s: Chol Khan, known in Russian sources as Shevkal or Shchelkan, was a Mongol envoy and a cousin of Özbeg, khan of the Golden Horde. In 1327 the violence of his retinue in Tver provoked a popular rising in which he and his men were killed. Özbeg sent a punitive army, joined by…

cherdyn.s: Cherdyn is an old town in Perm Krai, Russia, on the Kolva river west of the northern Urals. First recorded in 1451, it was the centre of the principality of Great Perm, conquered by Moscow in 1472, and remained a hub of the fur trade and of the route to Siberia until the…

cheyenne.s: The Cheyenne are an Algonquian-speaking Indigenous people of the Great Plains, who moved west from the upper Mississippi region and took up a horse-based bison-hunting life in the 18th century. Allied with the Lakota, they fought the United States in the wars of the 1860s and…

chernyakhov-culture.s: The Chernyakhov culture is an archaeological culture of the 3rd and 4th centuries CE, spread across present-day Ukraine, Moldova and parts of Romania. Known from large unfortified villages, cemeteries and wheel-made pottery, it is generally linked to the Goths, including the…

chamorro-people.s: The Chamorro are the indigenous people of the Mariana Islands, including Guam, whose ancestors settled the islands about 3,500 years ago. They built latte stone house foundations and lived by fishing and farming.

canete-river.s: The Cañete River flows from the Andes to the Pacific Ocean south of Lima, Peru, and its irrigated valley has been farmed for thousands of years. Before the Inca conquest it was the seat of the lordship of Guarco, which resisted the Incas for several years.

champaner.s: Champaner is a historic city at the foot of Pavagadh hill in Gujarat, India. Mahmud Begada of the Gujarat Sultanate took it from its Chauhan Rajput rulers in 1484 and rebuilt it as his capital, with mosques such as the Jami Masjid.

curse-of-agade.s: The Curse of Agade is a Sumerian literary composition, probably of the late 3rd millennium BCE, explaining the fall of the city of Akkad. It tells how King Naram-Sin offended the god Enlil by destroying his temple at Nippur, and how Enlil sent the Gutians from the mountains to…

carmona.s: Carmona is a town on a ridge east of Seville in Andalusia, Spain. An ancient settlement of the Tartessians and Romans, it was a fortified town of al-Andalus, held by the Banu Hajjaj in the late 9th century and the centre of the Birzalid taifa in the 11th century.

cog-ship.s: The cog was a type of sailing ship used in northern Europe from the 10th to the 14th century, with a flat bottom, high straight sides, a single square sail and, later, a stern rudder and raised castles. Large and cheap to build, it carried bulk cargoes such as grain, timber…

chamadevi.s: Chamadevi was the legendary first ruler of Hariphunchai, the Mon kingdom centred on Lamphun in northern Thailand. Northern Thai chronicles describe her as a princess of Lavo (Lopburi) invited by hermit founders to rule the new city, traditionally in the 7th century, bringing…

caddo.s: The Caddo are a Native American people of the region where Texas, Louisiana, Arkansas and Oklahoma meet, descended from the mound-building Caddoan Mississippian culture. Historically they formed three confederacies, the Hasinai, Kadohadacho and Natchitoches, and lived by maize…

cevennes.s: The Cévennes are a mountain range on the south-eastern edge of the Massif Central in France. Julius Caesar crossed them in deep snow in 52 BCE to surprise the Arverni.

clearchus-of-heraclea.s: Clearchus was tyrant of Heraclea Pontica on the Black Sea coast of Anatolia from 364 BCE until his assassination in 352 BCE. Recalled from exile to support the oligarchs, he seized power with mercenaries and ruled harshly.

citadel-of-the-ho-dynasty.s: The Citadel of the Ho Dynasty, or Tây Đô, is a stone citadel in Thanh Hóa province, Vietnam, built in 1397 by Hồ Quý Ly as a new capital. Its walls are made of huge cut limestone blocks fitted without mortar.

chris-patten.s: Chris Patten is a British Conservative politician who was the 28th and last governor of Hong Kong, from 1992 to 1997. He introduced electoral reforms that widened the franchise for the Legislative Council, angering Beijing, and presided over the handover of the colony to China…

chennakeshava-temple-belur.s: The Chennakeshava temple at Belur in Karnataka, India, is a Hindu temple dedicated to Vishnu, consecrated in 1117 by the Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana. Built of soapstone on a star-shaped platform, it is covered with finely carved friezes, bracket figures and sculpture.

chichimeca.s: Chichimeca was a Nahuatl name for the nomadic and semi-nomadic peoples of northern Mexico, and also for migrants from the north who settled in central Mexico. Several Nahua city-states, including Tenochtitlan and Texcoco, claimed Chichimec ancestry.

connemara.s: Connemara is a region of western County Galway, Ireland, between Lough Corrib and the Atlantic. A land of bogs, lakes and mountains such as the Twelve Bens, it was ruled by the O'Flaherty lords of Iar Connacht in the late Middle Ages.

cortes-of-tomar.s: The Cortes of Tomar was the assembly of the Portuguese estates held at Tomar in April 1581, which recognised Philip II of Spain as King Philip I of Portugal. In return Philip promised that Portugal would keep its own laws, offices, currency and colonial administration, and…

council-of-portugal.s: The Council of Portugal was the royal council created by Philip II of Spain in 1582 to advise the king on Portuguese affairs during the union of the crowns. Sitting at the court in Madrid and staffed by Portuguese, it handled appointments, petitions and government business for…

cambridgeshire.s: Cambridgeshire is a county in the East of England, with Cambridge as its county town. Its northern part lies in the Fens, a low-lying region drained from the 17th century onwards.

cinca.s: The Cinca is a river of Aragon in north-eastern Spain that rises in the central Pyrenees near Monte Perdido and flows south to join the Segre shortly before that river meets the Ebro. Its upper valley formed the medieval county of Sobrarbe, one of the cores of the Kingdom of…

carinthia.s: Carinthia is an Alpine region of southern Austria, centred on the Drava valley and the Klagenfurt basin, with a small part now in northern Slovenia. It grew from the early medieval Slavic principality of Carantania, became a duchy of the Holy Roman Empire in 976 and passed to…

carniola.s: Carniola is a historical region in present-day central Slovenia, centred on Ljubljana. Settled by Slavs in the early Middle Ages, it became a march and later a duchy of the Holy Roman Empire and passed to the Habsburgs in the 14th century.

conrad-of-sellenburen.s: Conrad of Sellenbüren was a Swiss nobleman who in 1120 founded the Benedictine abbey of Engelberg in a remote Alpine valley in central Switzerland, settling it with monks from Muri. He later entered the monastery himself and died in 1126.

cancor.s: Cancor was a Frankish count in the middle Rhine region in the 8th century. In 764 he and his mother Williswinda founded a monastery on their estate at Lorsch and placed it under their kinsman Chrodegang, bishop of Metz.

chrodegang-of-metz.s: Chrodegang was bishop of Metz from 742 until his death in 766 and a leading churchman of the early Carolingian kingdom under Pippin the Short. He wrote a rule for clergy living in community that became a model for cathedral canons, and he introduced Roman chant to the Frankish…

codex-aureus-of-st-emmeram.s: The Codex Aureus of St. Emmeram is an illuminated Gospel book written in gold ink, made in 870 for the Carolingian king Charles the Bald.

codex-argenteus.s: The Codex Argenteus, or Silver Bible, is a 6th-century manuscript of the Gospels in the Gothic translation made by Bishop Wulfila, written in silver and gold ink on purple parchment, probably in Ravenna under the Ostrogothic king Theodoric. It is the main surviving source for…

chetniks.s: The Chetniks were Serbian royalist and nationalist forces in occupied Yugoslavia during the Second World War, led by Draža Mihailović. They began as a resistance movement but fought Tito's Partisans and increasingly collaborated with Italian and German forces, and some units…

cisalpine-gaul.s: Cisalpine Gaul, 'Gaul this side of the Alps', was the Roman name for northern Italy between the Alps and the Apennines, settled by Celtic peoples such as the Insubres, Boii and Cenomani from the 5th and 4th centuries BCE. Rome conquered it in the late 3rd and early 2nd…

constitution-of-ireland.s: The Constitution of Ireland, Bunreacht na hÉireann, is the basic law of Ireland, drafted under Éamon de Valera and approved by referendum on 1 July 1937. It replaced the constitution of the Irish Free State, named the state Éire or Ireland, created the office of President and…

covenant-chain.s: The Covenant Chain was a series of alliances between the Iroquois Confederacy and the English colonies of North America, formalised at Albany in 1677. The colonies dealt with many other Native nations through the Iroquois, who claimed to speak for them, and the alliance was…

constitution-of-medina.s: The Constitution of Medina is a document attributed to Muhammad, drawn up soon after his emigration to Medina in 622. It defined the emigrants from Mecca, the Muslims of Medina and the town's Jewish tribes as one community, the umma, with mutual obligations of defence and…

charter-of-carnaro.s: The Charter of Carnaro was the constitution of the Italian Regency of Carnaro, proclaimed by Gabriele D'Annunzio in Fiume in September 1920 and drafted largely by the syndicalist Alceste De Ambris. It organised citizens into ten corporations, guaranteed broad civil rights…

christian-democracy-italy.s: Christian Democracy was a Catholic, centrist political party that dominated Italian politics from 1946 to 1994, leading or taking part in every government. Under Alcide De Gasperi it anchored Italy in NATO and European integration.

cork.s: Cork is the second-largest city in Ireland, on the River Lee in the south of the country. It grew from a monastery founded by Saint Finbarr in the 6th or 7th century and a later Viking settlement, and became the seat of the MacCarthy kings of Desmond before falling to the…

county-cork.s: County Cork is the largest county in Ireland, in the south-west of the province of Munster, named after the city of Cork. Its west has a deeply indented coast and in early medieval times was home to kingdoms of the Corcu Loigde and branches of the Eóganachta.

cankili-ii.s: Cankili II was the last king of Jaffna, in northern Sri Lanka, who seized power in 1617 as regent. He resisted the Portuguese with help from the Thanjavur Nayaks and Malabar privateers, but the Portuguese under Filipe de Oliveira conquered the kingdom in 1619.

charles-town-jamaica.s: Charles Town is a Maroon community in the parish of Portland in north-eastern Jamaica, near the coastal town of Buff Bay. It was settled by Windward Maroons after the peace of 1739, and its people still maintain Maroon traditions, land rights and governance under an elected…

cudjoe.s: Cudjoe was the leader of the Leeward Maroons of western Jamaica, communities of escaped enslaved Africans in the Cockpit Country. He led their resistance in the First Maroon War until, in 1739, he signed a treaty with the British governor Edward Trelawny that granted the…

cagliari.s: Cagliari is the capital and largest city of Sardinia, on its southern coast. Founded by the Phoenicians as Karalis, it was a Roman port and then the seat of the medieval Judicate of Cagliari.

camaldolese.s: The Camaldolese are a congregation of Benedictine monks founded by St Romuald at Camaldoli in Tuscany around 1012. They combine communal monastic life with hermit communities devoted to solitude and prayer.

cachar.s: Cachar is a district in the Barak valley of southern Assam, India, with its headquarters at Silchar. In the 18th century the Dimasa kings of the Kachari kingdom moved their capital to Khaspur in its plains, and the region took its name from them.

chandor.s: Chandor is a village in the Salcete area of South Goa, India, which as Chandrapura was an early capital of the Kadambas of Goa from the 10th century, and earlier of local rulers. Excavations have found the remains of an early temple there.

candi-belahan.s: Candi Belahan is an 11th-century bathing place on the eastern slope of Mount Penanggungan in East Java, Indonesia, traditionally linked with the burial of King Airlangga. Water flowed from fountains in the form of goddesses, and a celebrated statue of Vishnu riding Garuda…

chausath-yogini-temple-jabalpur.s: The Chausath Yogini Temple at Bheraghat near Jabalpur in central India is a circular open-air shrine of the 10th century built on a hill above the Narmada. Its cloister holds carved images of yoginis, female divinities of Tantric worship, around a later central shrine to Shiva…

central-java.s: Central Java is a province of Indonesia in the middle of the island of Java, with its capital at Semarang. Its volcanic plains were the heartland of early Javanese kingdoms, including the Medang Kingdom, builders of Borobudur and Prambanan in the 8th and 9th centuries, and…

chhachhrauli.s: Chhachhrauli is a town in the Yamunanagar district of Haryana, India. In the late 18th century it became the seat of the Sikh chiefs of Kalsia, descendants of Gurbakhsh Singh of the Karorsinghia misl, and remained the capital of the small princely state of Kalsia until it…

chitrakoot.s: Chitrakoot is a holy town on the border of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh in central India, in the Bundelkhand region. In the Ramayana it is the forest where Rama, Sita and Lakshmana spent part of their exile, and pilgrims walk round the sacred Kamadgiri hill.

candi-badut.s: Candi Badut is a Hindu temple near Malang in East Java, Indonesia, among the oldest surviving temples on the island. It is usually identified with the shrine to the sage Agastya described in the Dinoyo inscription of 760, built by King Gajayana of Kanjuruhan.

chigils.s: The Chigils were a Turkic tribe of Central Asia, recorded by Muslim geographers from the 10th century around Lake Issyk-Kul and the upper Chu valley. Closely linked to the Karluk confederation, they were one of the main tribal groups behind the Kara-Khanid Khanate and supplied…

chambal-river.s: The Chambal is a river of central India, rising in the Vindhya Range near Mhow in Madhya Pradesh and flowing north-east through Rajasthan to join the Yamuna. Its lower course runs through deeply eroded ravines that long sheltered outlaws, and part of it is protected as the…

cipollino-marble.s: Cipollino is a green-and-white banded marble quarried in antiquity near Karystos in southern Euboea, Greece. Its onion-like layers gave it its Italian name.

charles-de-foucauld.s: Charles de Foucauld was a French army officer and explorer who became a Catholic priest and hermit in the Sahara. From 1905 he lived among the Kel Ahaggar Tuareg at Tamanrasset, where he compiled a Tuareg dictionary and collected their poetry.

comilla.s: Comilla, officially Cumilla, is a city in south-eastern Bangladesh, near the Indian border with Tripura. The surrounding region was the heart of ancient Samatata, and the nearby Mainamati hills hold the ruins of Buddhist monasteries such as Shalban Vihara.

chuvash-people.s: The Chuvash are a Turkic people of the middle Volga, most of whom live in the Chuvash Republic of Russia, with its capital at Cheboksary. Their language is the only living member of the Oghur branch of Turkic, and they are widely seen as descendants of the Volga Bulgars.

cenel-neogain.s: The Cenél nEógain were a dynasty of the northern Uí Néill in Ireland, claiming descent from Eógan, son of Niall of the Nine Hostages. From their royal centre at Grianan of Aileach they dominated the kingdom of Ailech, held the high kingship in alternation with the southern Uí…

county-monaghan.s: County Monaghan is an inland county in the province of Ulster in the Republic of Ireland, with its county town at Monaghan. It was the heart of the MacMahon lordship of Oriel, the last part of the kingdom of Airgialla.

county-louth.s: County Louth is the smallest county in Ireland, on the east coast in the province of Leinster, with Dundalk and Drogheda as its main towns. Part of the kingdom of Airgialla in the 12th century, it was settled by the Anglo-Normans from the late 12th century and lay within the…

cypro-minoan-syllabary.s: The Cypro-Minoan syllabary is an undeciphered script used on Cyprus in the Late Bronze Age, from about 1550 to 1050 BCE. It developed from Linear A of Minoan Crete and is known from clay tablets, clay balls and inscribed objects found at Enkomi and other sites, as well as at…

charles-the-child.s: Charles the Child was a son of the West Frankish king Charles the Bald, who made him king of Aquitaine in 855 to win the Aquitanian nobility away from the rival Pippin II. His rule was contested and largely nominal, and he rebelled against his father in the early 860s.

chasseneuil-du-poitou.s: Chasseneuil-du-Poitou is a small town north of Poitiers in western France. It is usually identified with Cassinogilum, the Carolingian royal residence where Louis the Pious, son of Charlemagne, was born in 778 while his father was campaigning in Spain, and which served as one…

cortes.s: The Cortes were the representative assemblies of the Iberian kingdoms, in which the king met the clergy, nobility and towns to grant taxes, hear grievances and swear to uphold the laws. That of León in 1188 is among the earliest European parliaments to include town…

clan-donald.s: Clan Donald is a Scottish Highland clan descended from Domhnall, grandson of Somerled, King of the Isles. Its chiefs held the Lordship of the Isles from the 14th century until the title was forfeited to the Scottish crown in 1493, ruling the Hebrides and much of the western…

clan-macdougall.s: Clan MacDougall is a Scottish Highland clan descended from Dubhghall, eldest son of Somerled, King of the Isles. In the 13th century its chiefs were lords of Argyll and Lorn with castles such as Dunstaffnage, but they opposed Robert the Bruce, who defeated them at the Pass of…

clann-ruaidhri.s: Clann Ruaidhrí was a medieval kindred of the Hebrides and western Highlands descended from Ruaidhrí, grandson of Somerled. Its leaders held Garmoran, Uist and other lands and were among the leading sea-lords of the Isles in the 13th and 14th centuries.

cangas-de-onis.s: Cangas de Onís is a town in eastern Asturias, northern Spain, at the foot of the Picos de Europa. Tradition makes it the first seat of the Kingdom of Asturias, founded by Pelagius after his victory over a Muslim force at nearby Covadonga around 722, and the kings resided there…

coimbra.s: Coimbra is a city in central Portugal on the Mondego river. Roman Aeminium, it was taken from the Muslims in 878, lost to Almanzor in 987 and finally reconquered by Ferdinand I of León in 1064.

crinan-of-dunkeld.s: Crínán was the lay abbot of Dunkeld in Scotland in the early 11th century and the ancestor of the dynasty that ruled Scotland until 1286. He married Bethóc, daughter of King Malcolm II, and their son became King Duncan I.

cameroon-grassfields.s: The Cameroon Grassfields, or Western High Plateau, are the volcanic highlands of western Cameroon, covering the present North-West and West regions. A densely settled land of farms and savanna, they are home to many kingdoms and chiefdoms, such as Bamum, Bafut, Nso and…

charles-savage.s: Charles Savage was a European sailor who survived the wreck of the American brig Eliza in Fiji in 1808 and became one of the first beachcombers in the islands. Using muskets salvaged from the wreck, he fought for the chiefs of Bau, helping Naulivou extend Bau's power over its…

cilmeri.s: Cilmeri is a village near Builth Wells in Powys, Wales. On 11 December 1282 Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, the last native Prince of Wales, was killed nearby in a clash with English forces, and his death led to Edward I's conquest of Wales.

comoe-river.s: The Comoé is a river of West Africa, about 1,160 kilometres long, that rises in south-western Burkina Faso and flows south through eastern Ivory Coast to the Gulf of Guinea near Grand-Bassam. Its upper basin, savanna country home to the Kulango and the kingdom of Buna,…

comana-cappadocia.s: Comana was an ancient temple city in Cappadocia, in the upper Saros (Seyhan) valley of southern Anatolia. It was famous for its sanctuary of the goddess Ma, whose high priest governed thousands of temple servants and ranked second only to the king of Cappadocia.

cillium.s: Cillium was a Roman town in the province of Byzacena, at the site of modern Kasserine in west-central Tunisia, still known for its triumphal arch and mausoleums. In 544 the Byzantine general Solomon was defeated and killed near it by Berber forces led by Antalas and his…

ceredig-ap-cunedda.s: Ceredig ap Cunedda is the legendary founder of the early Welsh kingdom of Ceredigion, which tradition says was named after him. Welsh genealogies make him a son of Cunedda, who came from the north in the 5th century to drive Irish settlers out of Wales, and give him the land…

cunedda.s: Cunedda is a figure of Welsh tradition said to have come with his sons from Manaw Gododdin, near the head of the Firth of Forth, in the 5th century to drive the Irish from north Wales. He is remembered as the founder of the royal dynasty of Gwynedd, and early Welsh kingdoms…

charax-spasinou.s: Charax Spasinou was an ancient port city at the head of the Persian Gulf, near modern Basra in southern Iraq. Founded as an Alexandria by Alexander the Great and refounded by Hyspaosines around 141 BCE, it was the capital of the kingdom of Characene and a hub of trade between…

cruithne-legendary-king.s: Cruithne is the legendary father of the Picts in medieval Irish and Pictish origin legends. His seven sons, Fib, Fidach, Fotla, Fortrenn, Cait, Ce and Circinn, were said to have given their names to the seven provinces of Pictland.

chloderic.s: Chloderic was the son of Sigibert the Lame, king of the Franks of Cologne, in the early 6th century. He fought for Clovis I against the Visigoths at Vouillé in 507.

conn-of-the-hundred-battles.s: Conn of the Hundred Battles is a legendary High King of Ireland, said to have reigned in the 2nd century CE. Medieval genealogists made him the ancestor of the Connachta, who gave their name to Connacht, and through them of the Uí Néill and other leading dynasties.

county-roscommon.s: County Roscommon is an inland county in the province of Connacht, in the west of Ireland, bounded on the east by the River Shannon. It contains Rathcroghan, the ancient royal site of Connacht, and in the Middle Ages it was the core territory left to the O'Conor kings after the…

chikka-vira-rajendra.s: Chikka Vira Rajendra was the last raja of Coorg (Kodagu), in south-western India, reigning from 1820 to 1834. Accused of misrule and hostility to the British, he was deposed by an East India Company force in 1834, and Coorg was annexed.

cervione.s: Cervione is a hill village in the Castagniccia region of north-eastern Corsica, above the eastern coastal plain. It was long the residence of the bishops of Aleria, with a cathedral dedicated to Saint Erasmus.

croatian-hungarian-settlement.s: The Croatian–Hungarian Settlement, or Nagodba, was the agreement of 1868 that defined the place of Croatia-Slavonia within the Kingdom of Hungary after the Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867. Croatia-Slavonia kept its own Sabor and control of internal affairs, justice,…

croat-serb-coalition.s: The Croat–Serb Coalition was an alliance of Croatian and Serbian parties in Croatia-Slavonia and Dalmatia formed in 1905, following the Rijeka and Zadar resolutions. It promoted cooperation between Croats and Serbs against Hungarian and Austrian domination and held a majority…

croatian-academy-of-sciences-and-arts.n: Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts
croatian-academy-of-sciences-and-arts.s: The Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts is Croatia's national academy, founded in Zagreb in 1866 as the Yugoslav Academy of Sciences and Arts on the initiative of Bishop Josip Juraj Strossmayer, with the historian Franjo Rački as its first president. It published historical…

cornelius-fuscus.s: Cornelius Fuscus was a Roman equestrian who served as praetorian prefect under the emperor Domitian. In 86 or 87 CE he led a Roman army across the Danube into Dacia to punish King Decebalus for raids into Moesia, but he was killed and his army destroyed, possibly at Tapae.

chandrabhanu.s: Chandrabhanu Sridhamaraja was a king of Tambralinga on the Malay Peninsula in the 13th century, known from an inscription at Chaiya dated 1230. He built up a navy and invaded Sri Lanka twice, in 1247 and again around 1260, seeking among other things its Buddhist relics, and…

cardigan-wales.s: Cardigan is a market town in Ceredigion, west Wales, near the mouth of the River Teifi. Its castle, rebuilt in stone by Rhys ap Gruffydd, the Lord Rhys, was the scene of the first recorded eisteddfod in 1176.

cyfraith-hywel.s: Cyfraith Hywel, the law of Hywel, was the native law of medieval Wales, traditionally said to have been codified under Hywel Dda in the 10th century. Surviving in law books in Welsh and Latin from the 13th century, it set rules on inheritance, compensation for killing and…

copenhagen.s: Copenhagen is the capital and largest city of Denmark, on the island of Zealand facing the Øresund. A fishing and trading settlement fortified by Bishop Absalon in the 1160s, it became the royal residence and capital in the 15th century and grew rich on Baltic trade and the…

carbery-county-cork.s: Carbery is a region of south-west County Cork, Ireland, along the coast between Kinsale and Mizen Head. In the later Middle Ages it was ruled by the MacCarthy Reagh, a branch of the MacCarthy kings of Desmond, and its name survives in the baronies of East and West Carbery.

cormacs-chapel.s: Cormac's Chapel is a Romanesque chapel on the Rock of Cashel in County Tipperary, Ireland, built by Cormac Mac Carthaigh, king of Desmond, and consecrated in 1134. With its carved doorways, twin towers and painted interior, it is the finest early Romanesque church in Ireland.

chandrasuriya.s: Chandrasuriya is a king of Dhanyawadi in Arakan, western Myanmar, known from Arakanese tradition. The chronicles say that the Buddha visited his kingdom and that the Mahamuni image was cast in the Buddha's likeness during his reign, an account that is legendary rather than…

christ-church-cathedral-dublin.s: Christ Church Cathedral is the medieval cathedral of Dublin, founded around 1030 by the Norse king Sitric Silkbeard and Dúnán, the first bishop of Dublin. The Anglo-Normans rebuilt it in stone from the 1180s, and it is now the cathedral of the Church of Ireland's diocese of…

criccieth.s: Criccieth is a small town on Tremadog Bay in Gwynedd, north-west Wales, in the old district of Eifionydd. Its castle was built by Llywelyn the Great in the 1230s and was taken and strengthened by Edward I after his conquest of Wales in 1283.

chaonians.s: The Chaonians were one of the three main tribal groups of ancient Epirus, with the Molossians and Thesprotians, living in the north-west of the region along the Ionian coast. Once the leading people of Epirus, they joined the Molossian-led alliance and later the Epirote League.

cedd.s: Cedd was a Northumbrian monk trained at Lindisfarne who led a mission to the Middle Angles in 653 and then reconverted the East Saxons as their bishop. He founded churches at Bradwell-on-Sea and Tilbury and the monastery of Lastingham in Yorkshire, and acted as interpreter at…

cathal-mac-maghnusa.s: Cathal Óg Mac Maghnusa was an Irish churchman and scholar of Fermanagh, dean of Lough Erne and a canon of Armagh. At his home on Belle Isle in Upper Lough Erne he directed the compilation of the Annals of Ulster, one of the main sources for early and medieval Irish history.

cu-chonnacht-maguire.s: Cú Chonnacht Maguire was lord of Fermanagh, succeeding his brother Hugh Maguire after Hugh's death in 1600 during the Nine Years' War. In 1607 he arranged the ship that carried the earls of Tyrone and Tyrconnell into exile in the Flight of the Earls, sailing with them, and he…

cape-coast-castle.s: Cape Coast Castle is a fort on the coast of Ghana, first built by the Swedes in 1653 as Carolusborg and taken by the English in 1664. It became the headquarters of English and then British trade and government on the Gold Coast, holding enslaved Africans in its dungeons before…

caustantin-mac-fergusa.s: Caustantín mac Fergusa was king of the Picts from 789 to 820 and probably also controlled Dál Riata. He is traditionally credited with founding the church at Dunkeld, and the Dupplin Cross near Forteviot carries his name.

capetian-dynasty.s: The Capetian dynasty was the royal house of France descended from Hugh Capet, who became king in 987. Its direct line ruled until 1328, and its cadet branches, the Valois and the Bourbons, held the French throne until 1848, while other branches ruled Spain, Naples, Portugal…

cantigas-de-santa-maria.s: The Cantigas de Santa Maria are a collection of over 400 songs in Galician-Portuguese in praise of the Virgin Mary, compiled at the court of Alfonso X of Castile in the later 13th century. Most tell of miracles of the Virgin, and the illuminated manuscripts, with musical…

chelm.s: Chełm is a city in eastern Poland, near the Ukrainian border. Founded as Kholm by Daniel of Galicia in the 1230s, it became his capital and burial place, and it passed to Poland in the 14th century.

colombo.s: Colombo is the largest city and commercial capital of Sri Lanka, on the island's west coast. A Muslim trading port by the 14th century, it was fortified by the Portuguese in the early 16th century and taken by the Dutch in 1656 and the British in 1796, serving as the colony's…

catterick.s: Catterick is a town in North Yorkshire, England, near the Roman fort and town of Cataractonium on Dere Street. It is usually identified with Catraeth, the battle site mourned in the early Welsh poem Y Gododdin, and the nearby Catterick Garrison is the largest British Army base.

castle-rock-edinburgh.s: Castle Rock is the volcanic plug in central Edinburgh on which Edinburgh Castle stands. Occupied since the Bronze Age, it is identified with Din Eidyn, the stronghold of the British kingdom of Gododdin that fell to Northumbria in the 7th century, and it later became a royal…

caradog-ap-gruffydd.s: Caradog ap Gruffydd was a Welsh ruler of Gwent and Morgannwg in south-east Wales in the later 11th century, rising after the death of Gruffudd ap Llywelyn. Seeking to dominate south Wales, he was defeated and killed by Gruffudd ap Cynan and Rhys ap Tewdwr at the Battle of…

chepstow-castle.s: Chepstow Castle stands on a cliff above the River Wye in Monmouthshire, Wales. Begun by William FitzOsbern in 1067, it is the oldest surviving post-Roman stone fortification in Britain and was the base for Norman expansion into Gwent; it was later enlarged by the Marshal and…

cadwallon-ap-cadfan.s: Cadwallon ap Cadfan was a king of Gwynedd who, allied with Penda of Mercia, defeated and killed Edwin of Northumbria at the Battle of Hatfield Chase in 633. He then ravaged Northumbria for a year, killing Edwin's successors Osric and Eanfrith, until Oswald defeated and killed…

cap-haitien.s: Cap-Haïtien is a port on the north coast of Haiti. Founded by the French as Cap-Français, it was the wealthy capital of the colony of Saint-Domingue until 1770 and was burned in 1793 during the Haitian Revolution.

citadelle-laferriere.s: The Citadelle Laferrière is a mountaintop fortress near Milot in northern Haiti, built between about 1805 and 1820 by many thousands of workers on the orders of Henri Christophe. It was designed to resist an expected French attempt to reconquer Haiti and was armed with scores…

code-henry.s: The Code Henry was the legal code issued in 1812 by Henri Christophe for his Kingdom of Haiti in the north of the country. Based largely on French law, it covered civil, commercial, criminal and military matters, and included strict rules binding agricultural labourers to the…

crown-of-ireland-act-1542.s: The Crown of Ireland Act was passed by the Irish Parliament in June 1541, at the urging of Henry VIII, and created the title of King of Ireland for him and his successors. It replaced the Lordship of Ireland, held by English kings since the 12th century under a papal grant,…

campeche.s: Campeche is a state of Mexico on the western side of the Yucatán Peninsula, facing the Gulf of Mexico. Its interior holds major Maya sites such as Calakmul and Edzná, and its capital, the walled colonial port of San Francisco de Campeche, gave the state its name.

changsha.s: Changsha is the capital of Hunan province in south-central China, on the Xiang River. It was the capital of the Han-era Kingdom of Changsha, whose Mawangdui tombs yielded rich silk texts and paintings, and of the Ma family's Chu state in the 10th century.

church-of-the-holy-apostles-kars.n: Church of the Holy Apostles, Kars
church-of-the-holy-apostles-kars.s: The Church of the Holy Apostles is a 10th-century Armenian church in Kars, eastern Turkey, built by King Abas I of Bagratid Armenia between about 930 and 943. A domed tetraconch with reliefs of the twelve apostles on its drum, it served as the cathedral of the Bagratid capital.

casamance.s: The Casamance is the region of southern Senegal lying between The Gambia and Guinea-Bissau, drained by the Casamance River. Its name is traditionally derived from Kasa Mansa, the title of the king of the Bainuk kingdom of Kasa whom the Portuguese met in the 15th century.

cortes-of-leon-of-1188.s: The Cortes of León of 1188 was an assembly summoned by King Alfonso IX of León at the start of his reign, at which elected representatives of the towns sat for the first time alongside nobles and bishops. Its decrees guaranteed justice and the protection of property and…

county-laois.s: County Laois is an inland county in the Irish midlands, in the province of Leinster. It takes its name from the Loígis, whose kingdom was confiscated under Mary I and shired in 1556 as Queen's County, part of the first English plantation in Ireland together with neighbouring…

caranus-of-macedon.s: Caranus was, according to later Greek writers such as Theopompus and Diodorus, the founder of the Argead royal house of Macedon, a descendant of Heracles from Argos, traditionally dated to the 9th or 8th century BCE. Herodotus and Thucydides do not mention him and name…

cheitharol-kumbaba.s: The Cheitharol Kumbaba is the royal chronicle of Manipur, kept by court scribes in the Meitei language and script. It records the reigns of the kings of the Ningthouja dynasty year by year, beginning with Nongda Lairen Pakhangba, traditionally in 33 CE, and continuing into the…

chisumphi.s: Chisumphi is the high god of the Chewa people of Malawi and neighbouring parts of Zambia and Mozambique, associated with rain and fertility. His cult was served by rain shrines, the most important at Msinja, staffed by priestesses and spirit wives.

catualda.s: Catualda was a Germanic noble of the Gutones who had been exiled by Maroboduus, king of the Marcomanni. With Roman encouragement he invaded the Marcomannic kingdom in 19 CE, took the royal seat and forced Maroboduus to flee to Roman territory.

cleopatra-selene-ii.s: Cleopatra Selene II was the daughter of Cleopatra VII of Egypt and Mark Antony, born in 40 BCE as the twin of Alexander Helios. After her parents' deaths she was raised in Rome by Octavia and around 25 BCE married Juba II, becoming queen of Mauretania.

caesarea-mauretaniae.s: Caesarea, ancient Iol and modern Cherchell in Algeria, was a port on the Mediterranean coast west of Algiers. Originally a Phoenician and Carthaginian trading post, it was rebuilt by Juba II as the capital of the Kingdom of Mauretania and renamed in honour of Augustus.

cadair-idris.s: Cadair Idris is a mountain in Gwynedd, north-west Wales, rising to 893 metres at Penygadair at the southern end of Snowdonia National Park. Its name, 'chair of Idris', refers to a legendary giant or to Idris ap Gwyddno, a 7th-century king of Meirionnydd.

cardigan-bay.s: Cardigan Bay is a large bay of the Irish Sea on the west coast of Wales, stretching from the Llŷn Peninsula in the north to Strumble Head in Pembrokeshire. Its coast includes Aberystwyth, Aberaeron and Barmouth, and its waters are known for bottlenose dolphins.

creoda-of-mercia.s: Creoda is named in Anglo-Saxon royal genealogies as an early king of Mercia, a great-grandson of Icel, the father of Pybba and the grandfather of Penda. Later chronicles place his reign in the late 6th century, around 585 to 593, but no contemporary record survives, and he is…

clonard-abbey.s: Clonard Abbey was a monastery in County Meath, Ireland, founded by Finnian of Clonard in the early 6th century. It became one of the great schools of early Irish Christianity, and tradition makes its founder the teacher of the 'Twelve Apostles of Ireland', including Columba.

colman-mor.s: Colmán Már was a 6th-century Irish dynast of the southern Uí Néill, a son of the high king Diarmait mac Cerbaill. He was the ancestor of Clann Cholmáin, which by the 8th century became the dominant line of the kings of Mide and supplied several high kings of Ireland, including…

county-westmeath.s: County Westmeath is an inland county in the Irish midlands, in the province of Leinster, with Mullingar as its county town. It was created in 1543 from the western part of the Anglo-Norman lordship of Meath, itself formed from the early kingdom of Mide.

christmas-uprising.s: The Christmas Uprising was a revolt in Montenegro in early January 1919, around Orthodox Christmas, by supporters of independence and of the deposed King Nicholas I, known as the Greens. They opposed the Podgorica Assembly's decision of November 1918 to unite Montenegro with…

composition-of-connacht.s: The Composition of Connacht was a settlement of 1585 between the English government under the lord deputy Sir John Perrot and the lords of Connacht and Thomond. Gaelic lords gave up their traditional exactions in exchange for fixed rents to the crown and secure title to land…

cathal-mac-finguine.s: Cathal mac Finguine was king of Munster from about 721 until his death in 742, of the Eóganacht Glendamnach. He was the most powerful Munster king of his century, invading Leinster and Brega and challenging the Uí Néill high kings, and in 737 he met the high king Áed Allán to…

conall-corc.s: Conall Corc is the legendary ancestor of the Eóganachta, the ruling dynasties of Munster. Early Irish tales describe his exile in Pictland and his return to found the royal seat at Cashel, traditionally in the 5th century.

chikka-devaraja-wodeyar.s: Chikka Devaraja Wodeyar was king of Mysore from 1673 to 1704. He expanded the kingdom across southern Karnataka, bought Bangalore from the Mughals in 1689 and organised the administration into eighteen departments.

ceded-mile.s: The Ceded Mile was a strip of land about one mile deep along the north bank of the Gambia River, opposite Bathurst (Banjul), ceded by the king of Niumi to Britain in 1826. It allowed the British to command the river mouth, and Niumi's attempts to reverse the cession led to the…

celje.s: Celje is the third-largest city of Slovenia, on the Savinja River. As Celeia it was a Celtic settlement and then a Roman town of Noricum, granted municipal status under Emperor Claudius.

codex-amiatinus.s: The Codex Amiatinus is the oldest surviving complete manuscript of the Latin Vulgate Bible. It was made at the twin monastery of Wearmouth-Jarrow in Northumbria in the early 8th century, one of three great Bibles commissioned by Abbot Ceolfrith, who took it towards Rome as a…

christian-viii-of-denmark.s: Christian VIII was King of Denmark from 1839 to 1848. As Prince Christian Frederik, governor of Norway, he led Norwegian resistance to the transfer of Norway to Sweden by the Treaty of Kiel in 1814, convened the Eidsvoll assembly that adopted the Norwegian constitution and was…

chlodomer.s: Chlodomer was a Frankish king of the Merovingian dynasty, the second son of Clovis I and Clotilde. When his father's realm was divided in 511 he received lands along the Loire, ruling from Orléans.

clodoald.s: Clodoald, known as Saint Cloud, was a son of the Frankish king Chlodomer of Orléans. When his uncles Childebert I and Chlothar I murdered his brothers in 524 to seize their inheritance, he escaped, later renounced his claim and became a monk.

canice.s: Saint Canice, or Cainnech, was an Irish abbot and missionary of the 6th century, a companion of Columba. He founded the monastery of Aghaboe in Osraige and is said to have worked among the Picts in Scotland.

cerball-mac-dunlainge.s: Cerball mac Dúnlainge was king of Osraige in Ireland from about 842 until his death in 888. By fighting and allying with Viking leaders, and by exploiting rivalries between the kings of Munster and the Uí Néill, he made his small kingdom a major power.

corylas.s: Corylas was a ruler of Paphlagonia around 400 BCE, mentioned by Xenophon in the Anabasis. When the Greek mercenaries of the Ten Thousand marched along the Black Sea coast in 400 BCE, he sent envoys to negotiate with them.

cankiri.s: Çankırı is a city in northern central Turkey. In antiquity, as Gangra, it was the inland seat of the kings of Paphlagonia and later a Roman city renamed Germanicopolis.

charibert-i.s: Charibert I was a Merovingian king of the Franks who ruled the kingdom of Paris from 561 to 567. The eldest surviving son of Chlothar I, he received the old kingdom of Childebert I with Paris as his capital when his father's lands were divided.

childebert-i.s: Childebert I was a Merovingian king of the Franks who ruled from Paris from 511 to 558. A son of Clovis I, he shared in the division of his father's realm, joined his brothers in the conquest of Burgundy and in murdering the sons of Chlodomer, and campaigned against the…

canu-heledd.s: The Canu Heledd is a cycle of early Welsh englyn poems, probably composed in the 9th or 10th century, in which the princess Heledd laments the death of her brother Cynddylan and the destruction of his court and lands by the English. The poems, including 'Stafell Gynddylan' on…

cynddylan.s: Cynddylan was a Welsh prince of the mid-7th century, remembered as ruler of the kingdom of Pengwern in the area of modern Shropshire. The Canu Heledd poems lament his death fighting the English and the burning of his hall.

cybele.s: Cybele was the mother goddess of Anatolia, worshipped by the Phrygians as Matar, 'Mother', often shown in rock-cut shrines in the highlands. Her cult spread to the Greek world and, in 204 BCE, to Rome, where she was honoured as the Magna Mater with the festival of the…

cyngen-ap-cadell.s: Cyngen ap Cadell was the last king of Powys of the old royal line, ruling from about 808 until 854. He raised the Pillar of Eliseg near Llangollen in honour of his great-grandfather Eliseg, who had won back land from the English.

carl-blegen.s: Carl Blegen was an American archaeologist who led the University of Cincinnati excavations at Troy from 1932 to 1938. In 1939 he discovered the Mycenaean palace at Pylos, the so-called Palace of Nestor, finding on the first day hundreds of Linear B tablets baked by the fire…

colwyn-bay.s: Colwyn Bay is a seaside town on the north coast of Wales, in Conwy county, within the area of the early medieval kingdom of Rhos. It grew rapidly as a resort after the arrival of the railway in the mid-19th century.

cuneglasus.s: Cuneglasus was a 6th-century British king denounced by Gildas in his De Excidio Britanniae, who called him the charioteer of the Bear's Stronghold and accused him of making war on his countrymen and on God. He is often identified with Cynlas Goch, a ruler of Rhos in north…

carol-ii-of-romania.s: Carol II was King of Romania from 1930 to 1940. Having renounced his rights to the throne in 1925, he returned in 1930 to displace his young son Michael, and in 1938 he abolished the political parties and set up a royal dictatorship.

camillo-benso-count-of-cavour.s: Camillo Benso, Count of Cavour, was the leading statesman of the Kingdom of Sardinia and the first prime minister of united Italy. As premier from 1852 he modernised Piedmont's economy, joined the Crimean War and, in the Plombières agreement of 1858, won Napoleon III's support…

charles-marie-david-de-mayrena.s: Charles-Marie David de Mayrena was a French adventurer who in 1888 proclaimed himself King Marie I of the Sedang in the Central Highlands of Vietnam. Having won over Sedang, Bahnar and Rengao chiefs with the help of Catholic missionaries, he issued titles and decorations and…

cardiganshire.s: Cardiganshire is a historic county on the west coast of Wales, on Cardigan Bay, today the county of Ceredigion. It took its name from the early medieval kingdom of Ceredigion, which was joined with Ystrad Tywi to form Seisyllwg, and was made a shire after Edward I's conquest…

cefalu-cathedral.s: Cefalù Cathedral is a Norman cathedral in the town of Cefalù on the north coast of Sicily, founded by Roger II in 1131. Its massive twin-towered front and the Byzantine mosaics of its apse, dominated by a great figure of Christ Pantocrator, are celebrated works of Norman…

constitutions-of-melfi.s: The Constitutions of Melfi were a law code issued by the Emperor Frederick II for the Kingdom of Sicily at Melfi in 1231. Drafted by the jurists of his court, they asserted the king's supreme authority, regulated officials, courts and professions such as medicine, and limited…

ceretic-guletic.s: Ceretic Guletic was a 5th-century British king of Alt Clut, the fortress on Dumbarton Rock, and an early ruler of what became the kingdom of Strathclyde. He is usually identified with Coroticus, the king whose soldiers seized newly baptised Irish Christians as slaves and to…

ceretic-of-elmet.s: Ceretic was the last known king of Elmet, a British kingdom in what is now West Yorkshire, England. The Historia Brittonum says that Edwin of Northumbria seized Elmet and expelled him, usually dated around 617, and the Annales Cambriae record his death about that time.

cumbric.s: Cumbric was the Brittonic Celtic language of the early medieval north of Britain, spoken in the kingdom of Strathclyde and in Cumbria. Closely related to Old Welsh, it is known mainly from place names and a few personal names and legal terms.

chertsey-abbey.s: Chertsey Abbey was a Benedictine abbey at Chertsey in Surrey, England, founded in 666 by Eorcenwald, later Bishop of London, and endowed by the sub-king Frithuwold. Sacked by the Vikings in the 9th century, it was refounded in the 10th century and became one of the richest…

caedwalla.s: Cædwalla was king of Wessex from about 685 to 688. In a short and violent reign he conquered Sussex, Surrey, Kent and the Isle of Wight, where Bede says he set out to wipe out the native population and had the two young brothers of King Arwald killed after their baptism.

catherine-of-hungary-queen-of-serbia.n: Catherine of Hungary, Queen of Serbia
catherine-of-hungary-queen-of-serbia.s: Catherine of Hungary was a daughter of King Stephen V of Hungary and the wife of Stefan Dragutin, King of Serbia. Through her, Dragutin received from her brother Ladislaus IV in 1284 the Banate of Macsó with Belgrade and the lands of Usora and Soli, which became the base of…

catherine-de-medici.s: Catherine de' Medici was an Italian noblewoman who became queen of France as the wife of Henry II and dominated French politics as mother of the kings Francis II, Charles IX and Henry III. As regent and adviser from 1560 she sought to balance Catholics and Protestants during…

clonmacnoise.s: Clonmacnoise is a ruined monastery on the River Shannon in County Offaly, Ireland, founded by Saint Ciarán around 545. It became one of Ireland's leading centres of learning, art and royal burial, and its remains include several churches, round towers and the carved Cross of…

county-longford.s: County Longford is a county in the Irish midlands, in the province of Leinster, with its county town at Longford. It roughly corresponds to the medieval lordship of Annaly, ruled by the O'Farrells, and was created as a county in the late 16th century.

cunimund.s: Cunimund was the last king of the Gepids, ruling from about 560 from the region of Sirmium. He fought the Lombards, but in 567 the Lombard king Alboin, allied with the Avars, defeated and killed him, ending the Gepid kingdom.

castle-rushen.s: Castle Rushen is a medieval castle at Castletown in the south of the Isle of Man. Begun under the Norse kings of Mann and the Isles around 1200 and enlarged in the following centuries, it later served as the seat of the Stanley lords of Mann.

chichester.s: Chichester is a cathedral city in West Sussex, southern England. It began as the Roman town of Noviomagus Reginorum, capital of the Regni, where an inscription names the client king Togidubnus.

councils-of-braga.s: The Councils of Braga were church councils held at Bracara Augusta, capital of the Suebic kingdom in Gallaecia. The first, in 561, condemned the Priscillianist heresy and settled church discipline after the Suebi's return to Catholicism; the second, in 572 under Martin of…

conall-gulban.s: Conall Gulban is the traditional ancestor of the Cenél Conaill, a son of Niall of the Nine Hostages in Irish genealogy. Tír Chonaill, the land of Conall, roughly the later County Donegal, was named after him, and later tradition says he was baptised by Saint Patrick.

chen-yonghua.s: Chen Yonghua was the chief minister of Zheng Jing, ruler of the Kingdom of Tungning on Taiwan. He organised a Chinese-style administration, settled soldiers on farmland and promoted salt-making and trade.

cavarus.s: Cavarus was the last king of the Celtic kingdom of Tylis in eastern Thrace in the late 3rd century BCE. Polybius praises him as a ruler of kingly character who protected merchants and helped mediate peace between Byzantium and Rhodes in 220 BCE.

celts.s: The Celts were the Iron Age peoples of Europe who spoke Celtic languages, spread from Iberia and the British Isles to the Danube and Anatolia. Associated with the Hallstatt and La Tène cultures, they sacked Rome around 390 BCE, invaded Greece in 279 BCE and settled in Galatia.

comontorius.s: Comontorius was the leader of a band of Celts who took part in the invasion of the Balkans in 279 BCE and then settled in eastern Thrace. According to Polybius, they founded a kingdom with its capital at Tylis around 277 BCE.

claude-schaeffer.s: Claude Schaeffer was a French archaeologist who directed the excavations of Ugarit at Ras Shamra in Syria from 1929 until 1970. His work uncovered the city's palaces, temples and archives, including the tablets in the Ugaritic alphabet.

cathair-mor.s: Cathair Mór is a legendary king of Leinster and High King of Ireland, placed by medieval tradition in the 2nd century. Many Leinster dynasties, including the Uí Failge and the Uí Cheinnselaig, claimed descent from his sons.

county-galway.s: County Galway is a county in the province of Connacht in the west of Ireland, with the city of Galway as its centre. It includes Connemara, the Aran Islands and Lough Corrib.

conchobar-mac-nessa.s: Conchobar mac Nessa is the legendary king of the Ulaid in the Ulster Cycle of Irish literature, ruling from Emain Macha. He appears in the Táin Bó Cúailnge and in the tragic tale of Deirdre, whom he sought to marry.

cu-chulainn.s: Cú Chulainn is the greatest hero of the Ulster Cycle of Irish legend, a nephew of King Conchobar mac Nessa. In the Táin Bó Cúailnge he defends Ulster single-handed against the army of Queen Medb of Connacht.

chera-perumals-of-makotai.s: The Chera Perumals of Makotai were a dynasty that ruled much of Kerala in south-west India from about 800 to the early 12th century, with their capital at Makotai, or Mahodayapuram, near present-day Kodungallur. Their copper-plate grants, such as the Syrian Christian plates of…

cerdic.s: Cerdic is named by the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle as the founder of the kingdom of Wessex. It says he landed in southern Britain with his son Cynric in 495 and took the kingship in 519, ruling until 534, and later West Saxon kings traced their descent from him.

cynric.s: Cynric is named by the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle as the son, or in some sources the grandson, of Cerdic and his successor as king of Wessex, ruling from 534 to 560. The Chronicle credits him with victories over the Britons at Old Sarum and Barbury and with taking the Isle of Wight…

cannstatter-wasen.s: The Cannstatter Wasen, or Cannstatter Volksfest, is a large autumn festival held on the Wasen meadows beside the Neckar at Bad Cannstatt in Stuttgart, Germany. King William I of Württemberg founded it in 1818 as an agricultural fair after the famine of 1816–1817, crowned by a…

chencang.s: Chencang was an ancient county in the Wei river valley of Shaanxi, China, near present-day Baoji. In 206 BCE Liu Bang's general Han Xin led the Han army by the Chencang route into Guanzhong, while openly repairing the plank roads as a feint, and defeated Zhang Han; the ruse…

coppergate.s: Coppergate is a street in the centre of York, England, whose name comes from the Old Norse for street of the cup-makers. Excavations there by the York Archaeological Trust from 1976 to 1981 uncovered the waterlogged remains of houses, workshops and many thousands of objects…

chingiz-aitmatov.s: Chingiz Aitmatov was a Kyrgyz writer, the best-known author of Soviet Central Asia, who wrote in both Kyrgyz and Russian. His novella Jamilia, published in 1958, brought him international fame, and The Day Lasts More Than a Hundred Years, published in 1980, introduced the…

coro-venezuela.s: Coro, formally Santa Ana de Coro, is a city in north-western Venezuela, the capital of Falcón state. Founded by Juan de Ampíes in 1527, it is one of the oldest Spanish towns in South America and was the first capital of the province of Venezuela and the base of the Welser colony.

conon.s: Conon was an Athenian admiral of the late 5th and early 4th centuries BCE. He escaped the Athenian defeat at Aegospotami in 405 BCE and took refuge in Cyprus, and later commanded a fleet for the Persian king.

ctesias.s: Ctesias of Cnidus was a Greek physician and historian of the late 5th and early 4th centuries BCE who served at the Persian court of Artaxerxes II. He wrote a history of Assyria and Persia, the Persica, and a work on India, the Indica, both now known only from fragments and…

chilarai.s: Chilarai, born Shukladhwaj, was the younger brother and general of the Koch king Nara Narayan in the 16th century. His rapid campaigns, which earned him a nickname comparing him to the kite, defeated the Ahom kingdom and, according to later chronicles, forced tribute from…

chirmiri.s: Chirmiri is a coal-mining town in the hills of northern Chhattisgarh, India, in the area of the former princely state of Korea, or Koriya. The coal seams around it were opened up in the 20th century and are worked by South Eastern Coalfields, and mining remains the basis of…

champawat.s: Champawat is a town in eastern Uttarakhand, India, in the Kumaon hills near the border with Nepal. Tradition holds that it was the first seat of the Chand dynasty of Kumaon, founded by Som Chand, before the capital moved to Almora in the 16th century.

chand-dynasty.s: The Chand dynasty ruled the hill kingdom of Kumaon, in modern Uttarakhand, India, until the Gorkha conquest of 1790. Tradition traces it to Som Chand, a Rajput prince from the plains who settled at Champawat, though its early chronology is legendary.

corippus.s: Flavius Cresconius Corippus was a Latin poet from Roman North Africa in the 6th century. His epic Iohannis, in eight books, celebrates the campaigns of the Byzantine general John Troglita against the Moorish tribes in the 540s and is a chief source for the Laguatan and other…

changchun.s: Changchun is the capital of Jilin province in north-east China. It grew in the early 20th century as the junction between the Russian-controlled Chinese Eastern Railway and the Japanese South Manchuria Railway.

caroline-of-zweibrucken.s: Caroline of Zweibrücken, known as the Great Landgravine, was the wife of Landgrave Louis IX of Hesse-Darmstadt. While her husband stayed mostly at his garrison town of Pirmasens, she managed the court at Darmstadt and made it a meeting place for writers of the age of…

county-palatine-of-saxony.s: The County Palatine of Saxony was a medieval palatinate within the stem duchy of Saxony, whose counts palatine represented royal authority in the region around the Saale and Unstrut. It was held by the counts of Goseck and then of Sommerschenburg, and in 1180 passed to the…

chidambaram.s: Chidambaram is a temple town in Tamil Nadu, India, near the Coromandel coast. It is famous for the Thillai Nataraja Temple, dedicated to Shiva as the cosmic dancer Nataraja, one of the most sacred sites of Tamil Shaivism.

crown-of-thorns.s: The Crown of Thorns is a relic venerated as the crown placed on Jesus's head before the crucifixion. It was kept in Constantinople until Emperor Baldwin II of the Latin Empire, desperate for money, pawned it to Venetian merchants; Louis IX of France acquired it in 1238 and…

cocom.s: The Cocom were a Maya ruling lineage of northern Yucatán who dominated the city of Mayapan from the 13th century. According to colonial chronicles they were overthrown around 1441 by a revolt led by the Xiu, who killed most of the family and destroyed the city.

charles-wheler.s: Sir Charles Wheler, 2nd Baronet, was an English soldier and politician who sat in the House of Commons. In 1671 he became the first governor of the Leeward Islands after they were separated from Barbados.

cape-lefkatas.s: Cape Lefkatas is the southern tip of the island of Lefkada in the Ionian Sea, marked by high white cliffs that gave the island its name. In antiquity a temple of Apollo stood there, and legend held that the poet Sappho leapt to her death from the cliffs.

charles-taylor-liberia.s: Charles Taylor is a Liberian warlord and politician who launched the rebellion of 1989 that began the First Liberian Civil War and was president of Liberia from 1997 to 2003. He backed the Revolutionary United Front in Sierra Leone's civil war, and in 2012 the Special Court…

croatia.s: Croatia is a country in south-eastern Europe on the eastern Adriatic coast, with its capital at Zagreb. A medieval Croatian duchy became a kingdom around 925 and in 1102 entered a union with Hungary that lasted, under Habsburg rule from 1527, until 1918.

changu-narayan-temple.s: The Changu Narayan Temple is a Hindu temple of Vishnu on a hilltop near Bhaktapur in the Kathmandu Valley, Nepal. A stone pillar there bears the inscription of King Manadeva I dated 464 CE, the earliest dated inscription in Nepal.

convention-of-mombello.s: The Convention of Mombello was the agreement of 6 June 1797, made at Napoleon Bonaparte's headquarters in the villa of Mombello near Milan, under which the aristocratic Republic of Genoa was replaced by the democratic Ligurian Republic. It followed a pro-French rising in Genoa…

chillon-river.s: The Chillón is a river of Peru's central coast that flows from the Andes to the Pacific just north of Lima, its lower valley now part of the metropolitan area. Its valley was settled by the Lima culture, later by the Chancay culture and the Collique polity, and then by the…

cleobulus.s: Cleobulus was a tyrant of Lindos on Rhodes in the 6th century BCE, counted among the Seven Sages of Greece. Ancient tradition credits him with rebuilding the temple of Athena Lindia on the acropolis of Lindos and with sayings such as 'Moderation is best'.

cesis.s: Cēsis (German: Wenden) is a town in Vidzeme, northern Latvia. The Livonian Brothers of the Sword built a castle there in the early 13th century, which later became the residence of the master of the Livonian Order.

crispo-family.s: The Crispo family were the second dynasty of the Duchy of the Archipelago, the Latin state centred on Naxos in the Aegean. Francesco I Crispo seized the duchy in 1383 from the last of the Sanudo line, and his descendants ruled it, mostly under Venetian protection and later as…

castlereagh.s: Castlereagh is an area on the south-eastern edge of Belfast in Northern Ireland, named after the castle, in Irish An Caisleán Riabhach, 'the grey castle', that was the seat of the O'Neills of Clandeboye. The castle stood on high ground overlooking Belfast.

cia-degli-ubaldini.s: Cia degli Ubaldini was the wife of Francesco II Ordelaffi, lord of Forlì. During Cardinal Albornoz's campaign to restore papal rule in Romagna she commanded the defence of Cesena in 1357, holding out in the citadel until she was forced to surrender.

central-intelligence-agency.s: The Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) is the foreign intelligence service of the United States, created by the National Security Act of 1947. Besides gathering intelligence it carried out covert operations during the Cold War, including the 1953 coup in Iran that overthrew…

caerphilly-castle.s: Caerphilly Castle, north of Cardiff in south Wales, is a vast concentric castle begun in 1268 by Gilbert de Clare, Earl of Gloucester and lord of Glamorgan, to block the advance of Llywelyn ap Gruffudd. Surrounded by artificial lakes, it is the largest castle in Wales and one…

cardiff.s: Cardiff is the capital and largest city of Wales, on the Bristol Channel at the mouth of the Taff. Its castle was built around 1093 by Robert Fitzhamon inside a Roman fort and became the centre of the marcher lordship of Glamorgan.

castello-d-empuries.s: Castelló d'Empúries is a town in the Alt Empordà in north-eastern Catalonia, near the Gulf of Roses. In the Middle Ages it became the seat of the counts of Empúries, who built there a large Gothic church, the basilica of Santa Maria.

corinthia.s: Corinthia is a region of southern Greece around the Isthmus of Corinth, linking the Peloponnese with the mainland. Dominated by ancient Corinth and the citadel of Acrocorinth, it controlled the land route into the peninsula and the trade of two gulfs.

charlotte-stanley-countess-of-derby.s: Charlotte Stanley, Countess of Derby, born Charlotte de La Trémoille, was a French Huguenot noblewoman who married James Stanley, later 7th Earl of Derby, in 1626. During the English Civil War she held Lathom House against a parliamentary siege in 1644.

costanza-da-varano.s: Costanza da Varano was an Italian noblewoman and humanist writer from the Varano family of Camerino, admired for her Latin orations and letters. A granddaughter of Galeazzo Malatesta, lord of Pesaro, she married Alessandro Sforza in 1444, which led to his acquisition of Pesaro…

costanzo-i-sforza.s: Costanzo I Sforza was lord of Pesaro from 1473 to 1483, son of Alessandro Sforza and Costanza da Varano. A condottiero in the service of several Italian states, he began the Rocca Costanza fortress in Pesaro in 1474 and married Camilla d'Aragona.

cesena.s: Cesena is a city in Romagna, northern Italy, on the Savio river near the Adriatic. Ruled at times by the Ordelaffi and the Malatesta, it was the seat of Cesare Borgia's government as Duke of Romagna in 1501–1503.

castelvecchio-verona.s: Castelvecchio is a fortress in Verona built from 1354 by Cangrande II della Scala, together with the fortified Ponte Scaligero across the Adige. Later a barracks, it was restored in the 20th century and converted by the architect Carlo Scarpa into the Castelvecchio Museum.

chateau-clique.s: The Château Clique was the name given to the small group of wealthy English-speaking merchants, officials and seigneurs who dominated the appointed councils of Lower Canada in the early 19th century. Named after the governor's residence, the Château Saint-Louis in Quebec City,…

chelmno-extermination-camp.s: Chełmno extermination camp was the first Nazi extermination camp, set up in December 1941 at the village of Chełmno nad Nerem in German-occupied Poland, north-west of Łódź. Using gas vans, the SS murdered at least 150,000 people there, mostly Jews from the Łódź Ghetto and the…

cilento.s: The Cilento is a hilly region of southern Campania, Italy, in the province of Salerno between the Gulf of Salerno and the Gulf of Policastro. In antiquity it was home to the Greek cities of Poseidonia (Paestum) and Elea, later dominated by the Lucanians.

chones.s: The Chones were an ancient people of southern Italy, living near the Ionian coast of modern Basilicata and northern Calabria before the arrival of Greek colonists. Greek writers regarded them as related to the Oenotrians, and the land around Siris and Metapontum was called…

chucuito.s: Chucuito is a town on the western shore of Lake Titicaca in the Puno region of Peru. Before the Inca conquest it was the capital of the Aymara Lupaca kingdom, and under Spanish rule it was the centre of a large royal province.

cabeco-das-fraguas.s: Cabeço das Fráguas is a hill in the district of Guarda in central Portugal, crowned by an Iron Age hillfort. A rock inscription near its summit, written in the Latin alphabet around the turn of the eras, is one of the few known texts in the Lusitanian language.

circipanians.s: The Circipanians (Circipani) were a West Slavic tribe of the Lutician federation, living between the Recknitz and the Peene in modern Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Germany. Their name means 'those beyond the Peene'.

claudius.s: Claudius was Roman emperor from 41 to 54 CE, proclaimed by the Praetorian Guard after the murder of his nephew Caligula. His reign saw the invasion of Britain in 43 and the organisation of Mauretania, Lycia, Thrace and Judea as provinces, and he admitted Gallic nobles to the…

cinyps.s: The Cinyps was a river of ancient Libya, now the Wadi Caam (Wadi Ka'am), which reaches the Mediterranean east of Leptis Magna. Herodotus describes the fertile land along it, then held by the Macae.

cotabato-city.s: Cotabato City is a port on the Mindanao (Pulangi) River in the southern Philippines, the historic seat of the Sultanate of Maguindanao. Spain occupied it in 1861, and the Americans after 1899.

chungcheong-province.s: Chungcheong Province was one of the Eight Provinces of Joseon Korea, in the centre-west of the peninsula, divided in 1896 into North and South Chungcheong. In ancient times the area belonged to the Mahan confederacy and then to Baekje, whose later capitals Ungjin (Gongju) and…

chikunda.s: The Chikunda were slave soldiers and hunters of the Zambezi valley in Mozambique, originally the armed retainers of the Portuguese prazo estates. In the 19th century, after the prazo system collapsed, many served warlords such as the Pereira family of Makanga and the da Cruz…

cerro-del-villar.s: Cerro del Villar is an archaeological site at the mouth of the Guadalhorce river near Málaga in southern Spain, once an island in the river's estuary. Phoenicians founded a settlement there in the 8th century BCE, with houses, workshops and a busy harbour.

county-fermanagh.s: County Fermanagh is a county in the south-west of Northern Ireland, centred on the lakes of Lough Erne and the town of Enniskillen. It takes its name from the Fir Manach, an early medieval population group, and from the 13th century until the Plantation of Ulster it was ruled…

county-wexford.s: County Wexford is a county in the province of Leinster in south-eastern Ireland, named after its county town, Wexford, and bordered by the Irish Sea and St George's Channel. Its coast was among the first parts of Ireland taken by the Anglo-Normans from 1169.

catilinarian-conspiracy.s: The Catilinarian conspiracy was a plot by the Roman aristocrat Lucius Sergius Catilina (Catiline) and his associates to seize power in Rome in 63 BCE, after he had again failed to win election as consul. Exposed by the consul Cicero, whose four speeches against Catiline became…

congo-crisis.s: The Congo Crisis was the period of upheaval in the Republic of the Congo, now the Democratic Republic of the Congo, from its independence from Belgium in June 1960 to Mobutu Sese Seko's seizure of power in 1965. It began with an army mutiny, Belgian military intervention and…

chief-joseph.s: Chief Joseph was a leader of the Wallowa band of the Nez Perce people of the Pacific Northwest. When the United States government ordered his people onto a reservation in 1877, he and other leaders led some 800 Nez Perce on a fighting retreat of about 1,900 kilometres towards…

chavda-dynasty.s: The Chavda dynasty ruled northern Gujarat in western India from the 8th century until the mid-10th century. According to tradition its founder Vanaraja established the capital Anahilapataka (Patan) around 746.

cerro-de-hojas-jaboncillo.s: Cerro de Hojas-Jaboncillo is an archaeological complex on hills between Portoviejo and Montecristi in Manabí province, Ecuador. It was a major centre of the Manteño culture from about 800 to the Spanish conquest, with stone house foundations, terraces and the culture's…

casale-monferrato.s: Casale Monferrato is a town on the Po in Piedmont, north-western Italy. It became the capital of the marquisate of Montferrat in the 15th century and remained the main seat under the Gonzaga, who built a great citadel there around 1590.

canossa-castle.s: Canossa Castle is a ruined fortress in the Apennines south of Reggio Emilia, Italy, the seat of the house of Canossa, which held the March of Tuscany from 1027. In January 1077 Emperor Henry IV waited there for three days in the snow to obtain Pope Gregory VII's forgiveness,…

carnuntum.s: Carnuntum was a Roman legionary fortress and town on the Danube between Vienna and Bratislava, in present-day Lower Austria. Capital of the province of Pannonia Superior, it lay on the Amber Road and was a base for Marcus Aurelius in the Marcomannic Wars.

commodus.s: Commodus was Roman emperor from 180 to 192, son of Marcus Aurelius, with whom he had ruled jointly since 177. On his father's death he made peace with the Marcomanni and other Danubian peoples, ending the Marcomannic Wars.

colln.s: Cölln was a medieval town on an island in the Spree, the twin of Berlin on the opposite bank. Its first record, in 1237, is taken as the founding date of Berlin.

charles-margrave-of-burgau.s: Charles of Burgau was the son of Archduke Ferdinand II of Austria and Philippine Welser. Because of his parents' unequal marriage he could not inherit Tyrol, but he received the Margraviate of Burgau in Swabia and from 1609 resided at Günzburg.

cottbus.s: Cottbus (Lower Sorbian: Chóśebuz) is the second-largest city of Brandenburg, Germany, on the Spree in Lower Lusatia. It became part of Brandenburg in 1445 and later developed a strong textile industry.

czech-republic.s: The Czech Republic, or Czechia, is a landlocked country in central Europe made up of the historical lands of Bohemia, Moravia and Czech Silesia, with Prague as its capital. It became independent on 1 January 1993 after the peaceful dissolution of Czechoslovakia.

cicones.s: The Cicones were a Thracian people living on the northern Aegean coast near Ismarus and Maroneia. In Homer's Iliad they are allies of Troy, and in the Odyssey Odysseus sacks their town of Ismarus, where the priest Maron gives him the strong wine later used against the Cyclops.

charles-emmanuel-i-duke-of-savoy.n: Charles Emmanuel I, Duke of Savoy
charles-emmanuel-i-duke-of-savoy.s: Charles Emmanuel I was Duke of Savoy from 1580 to 1630, an ambitious ruler who sought to expand his state between France and Spain. He seized the Marquisate of Saluzzo in 1588 and kept it by the Treaty of Lyon in 1601, giving up Bresse and Bugey to France.

chieti.s: Chieti is a city in Abruzzo, central Italy, on a hill above the Pescara river near the Adriatic. As Teate it was the main town of the Italic Marrucini and later a Roman municipium, with temples, baths and a theatre.

cirta.s: Cirta was the capital of the Numidian kingdom, on a rocky plateau above the Rhumel gorge in north-eastern Algeria. It was a royal seat of Syphax and then of Masinissa and his heirs, and Jugurtha's massacre of Italian traders there in 112 BCE led to war with Rome.

chidiaonga.s: Chidiaonga was a leader of the Maseko Ngoni in the nineteenth century. After the death of Mputa, under whom the Maseko had moved north to the Songea area of southern Tanzania and been driven back, he led them into the highlands south-west of Lake Malawi, where they settled…

capussa.s: Capussa was a king of the Massylii, a Numidian people of North Africa, in the late third century BCE. The son of Oezalces, who had succeeded his brother Gaia, he took the throne on his father's death but was soon killed in a civil war by the noble Mazaetullus, who set up…

cherchell.s: Cherchell is a coastal town in Algeria, west of Algiers. Founded as the Phoenician and Punic port of Iol, it was renamed Caesarea by Juba II, who made it the capital of his Mauretanian kingdom in 25 BCE.

chhau-dance.s: Chhau is a tradition of martial and folk dance from eastern India, performed in three main styles, Purulia in West Bengal, Seraikela in Jharkhand and Mayurbhanj in Odisha. Danced mainly at the spring festival of Chaitra Parva, it enacts episodes from the epics and local…

canggal-inscription.s: The Canggal inscription is a Sanskrit inscription dated 732 CE, found on Mount Wukir near Magelang in Central Java. It records the erection of a Shiva lingam by King Sanjaya and praises his rule over Java.

cylon-of-athens.s: Cylon was an Athenian noble and Olympic victor who tried to make himself tyrant of Athens, probably in 632 BCE, with help from his father-in-law Theagenes, tyrant of Megara. The coup failed; Cylon escaped, but his followers were killed after taking sanctuary, and the curse…

chronicle-of-the-morea.s: The Chronicle of the Morea is a fourteenth-century history of the Frankish Principality of Achaea in the Peloponnese, surviving in Greek, French, Aragonese and Italian versions. It covers the conquest after the Fourth Crusade, the reigns of the Villehardouin princes and the…

cassel-nord.s: Cassel is a small town in the Nord department of northern France, on a hill rising above the Flemish plain. In Roman times it was Castellum Menapiorum, the capital of the Menapii, and roads radiated from it across the region.

cavallino.s: Cavallino is a town just south-east of Lecce in Apulia, southern Italy. It is the site of one of the main Messapian settlements of the Salento peninsula, a large walled town with houses and tombs that flourished in the sixth century BCE before being abandoned early in the fifth.

claudia-sheinbaum.s: Claudia Sheinbaum is a Mexican scientist and politician who became the first woman president of Mexico on 1 October 2024. Trained as an energy engineer, she served as environment secretary of Mexico City under Andrés Manuel López Obrador and then as head of government of the…

concession-of-evoramonte.s: The Concession of Evoramonte was the agreement of 26 May 1834 that ended the Liberal Wars in Portugal. Defeated by the liberal forces of Pedro IV, the absolutist Miguel I surrendered at Evoramonte in the Alentejo, gave up his claim to the throne and went into permanent exile,…

chemosh.s: Chemosh was the national god of the Moabites, the people of the Iron Age kingdom of Moab east of the Dead Sea. The Mesha Stele, inscribed in the 9th century BCE, attributes Israel's domination of Moab to his anger and Mesha's victories to his favour.
