caramansa.s: Caramansa was a ruler on the Gold Coast, in present-day Ghana, with whom the Portuguese commander Diogo de Azambuja negotiated in January 1482 for permission to build a fortress at Elmina. Portuguese chronicles describe the ceremonial meeting and the chief's reluctant consent.

cacheu.s: Cacheu is a town on the Cacheu river in north-western Guinea-Bissau, founded by the Portuguese in 1588 as a fortified trading post. It was one of the oldest European settlements in West Africa and a major centre of the Atlantic slave trade, dominated by Luso-African traders.

cockacoeske.s: Cockacoeske was a Pamunkey leader who ruled as weroansqua from 1656 until her death in 1686. Widow of the chief Totopotomoy, she sought to restore Pamunkey authority over the former Powhatan peoples, and she signed the Treaty of Middle Plantation in 1677, which made the tribes…

cynllaith.s: Cynllaith was a medieval commote in north-east Wales, in the valley of the River Cynllaith on the borders of modern Powys and Wrexham. It formed part of Powys Fadog, and its lordship was later held by Owain Glyndŵr, whose principal house stood at Sycharth within it.

castell-dinas-bran.s: Castell Dinas Brân is a ruined medieval castle on a steep hill above Llangollen in north-east Wales. It was built around 1260 by Gruffydd ap Madog, prince of Powys Fadog, on the site of an Iron Age hillfort.

campania.s: Campania is a region of southern Italy on the Tyrrhenian Sea, with Naples as its capital. Its fertile volcanic plain drew Greek colonists, Etruscans and Samnites, and Rome won control of it in the 4th century BCE.

corbie-abbey.s: Corbie Abbey was a Benedictine monastery in Picardy, northern France, founded around 657 by Queen Balthild. Under the Carolingians it became a leading centre of learning and manuscript copying, where an early form of Caroline minuscule script was used.

cambodunum.s: Cambodunum was a Roman town on the Iller in the province of Raetia, on the site of modern Kempten in Bavaria. Mentioned by Strabo, it was among the earliest Roman towns north of the Alps and had a forum, baths and temples.

cunigunde-of-luxembourg.s: Cunigunde of Luxembourg was the wife of Emperor Henry II and was crowned empress in 1014. She acted as regent after his death in 1024 and then retired to the convent of Kaufungen, which she had founded.

council-of-basel.s: The Council of Basel was a general council of the Catholic Church that met at Basel from 1431, continuing the conciliar movement. It made peace with the moderate Hussites but clashed with Pope Eugene IV, who moved the council to Ferrara in 1437; the members who stayed deposed…

chur.s: Chur is the capital of the canton of Graubünden in eastern Switzerland, on the Rhine near the routes to the Alpine passes. Its bishops, recorded from 451, ruled much of the region until the Ilanz Articles of the 1520s, and the town led the League of God's House within the…

corbinian.s: Corbinian was a Frankish missionary bishop who worked at Freising in Bavaria around 720 and is regarded as the founder of its diocese. According to legend, a bear killed his pack horse on the road to Rome and was made to carry his baggage, and the 'Corbinian bear' appears in…

christian-the-younger-of-brunswick.s: Christian the Younger of Brunswick was a German Protestant commander in the Thirty Years' War and administrator of the prince-bishopric of Halberstadt from 1616. Champion of the exiled Elizabeth Stuart, he raised armies for the Palatine cause, but was defeated at Höchst in…

cristoforo-madruzzo.s: Cristoforo Madruzzo was prince-bishop of Trent from 1539 to 1567, later also bishop of Brixen, and a cardinal from 1542. He was host of the Council of Trent, which met in his city between 1545 and 1563, and he acted as an intermediary between the papacy and the Emperor Charles V.

congress-of-lushnje.s: The Congress of Lushnjë was a national assembly of Albanian delegates held at Lushnjë from 28 to 31 January 1920. Meeting while foreign troops occupied parts of the country and the great powers discussed its partition, it rejected any division of Albania, set up a regency…

charles-i-duke-of-mantua.s: Charles I Gonzaga was Duke of Nevers and Rethel in France and from 1627 Duke of Mantua and Montferrat. In 1606 he founded the planned town of Charleville on the Meuse as the capital of his sovereign principality of Arches.

conde-sur-lescaut.s: Condé-sur-l'Escaut is a small town in the Nord department of France, where the Haine flows into the Scheldt near the Belgian border. In the Middle Ages it belonged to the County of Hainaut.

cyril-of-white-lake.s: Cyril of White Lake was a Russian monk and saint. A monk of the Simonov Monastery in Moscow, he left in 1397 for the remote north, where he founded a monastery on the Siverskoye lake near Beloozero.

cherven-towns.s: The Cherven Towns were a group of fortified settlements in the borderland between Poland and Kievan Rus', in the area of present-day south-eastern Poland and western Ukraine, named after the stronghold of Cherven. The Primary Chronicle records that Vladimir I took them from…

capetian-house-of-anjou.s: The Capetian House of Anjou was a branch of the French royal family founded by Charles of Anjou, brother of Louis IX. Charles conquered the Kingdom of Sicily in 1266 but lost the island in the Sicilian Vespers of 1282, after which his descendants ruled the Kingdom of Naples…

casilinum.s: Casilinum was an ancient town in Campania, southern Italy, at a crossing of the Volturno river on the Via Appia. It is remembered for its resistance to Hannibal, who besieged it in 216 and 215 BCE.

castiglione-delle-stiviere.s: Castiglione delle Stiviere is a town in the province of Mantua in Lombardy, Italy, south of Lake Garda. It was ruled by a branch of the Gonzaga family as a marquisate and principality, and was the birthplace of Saint Aloysius Gonzaga.

chirchiq-river.s: The Chirchiq is a river in Uzbekistan and southern Kazakhstan, a right tributary of the Syr Darya, about 155 kilometres long. It is formed by the Pskem and Chatkal rivers, which meet in the Charvak reservoir in the western Tian Shan.

congress-of-erfurt.s: The Congress of Erfurt was a meeting between Napoleon and Tsar Alexander I of Russia held in Erfurt from 27 September to 14 October 1808, attended by many German princes. It was meant to renew the alliance agreed at Tilsit, but Alexander would not commit himself against…

chameria.s: Chameria is a coastal region of Epirus in north-western Greece and the far south of Albania, lying roughly between the Kalamas river and Butrint. Albanian clans settled there in the late Middle Ages, and it formed part of the Despotate of Epirus and later of Ottoman Epirus.

clausthal-zellerfeld.s: Clausthal-Zellerfeld is a town in the Upper Harz of Lower Saxony, Germany, formed in 1924 from the mining towns of Clausthal and Zellerfeld. Silver and lead mining there flourished from the 16th century, making it the centre of the Upper Harz mining district, and its mining…

charles-anthony-prince-of-hohenzollern.s: Charles Anthony was the last sovereign Prince of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen, from 1848, and ceded his principality to Prussia in 1849–1850. He served as Prussian minister-president from 1858 to 1862 during the liberal 'New Era' of the regency of William I.

carl-3rd-prince-of-leiningen.s: Carl, 3rd Prince of Leiningen, was the son of Prince Emich Carl and Princess Victoria of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld, whose second marriage, to the Duke of Kent, produced Queen Victoria, his half-sister. A mediatised prince with his seat at Amorbach, he served briefly in 1848 as the…

cesky-krumlov.s: Český Krumlov, in German Krumau, is a town in South Bohemia, Czech Republic, set in tight bends of the Vltava. Its castle, one of the largest in the country, was the seat of the Rosenberg family, then of the Eggenbergs, and from 1719 of the princes of Schwarzenberg, who kept…

charlotte-de-la-marck.s: Charlotte de La Marck was the heiress of the La Marck family's principality of Sedan and duchy of Bouillon. In 1591 she married Henri de La Tour d'Auvergne, a Protestant ally of Henry IV, and when she died childless in 1594 she left him her lands, which passed to the La Tour…

caslav-klonimirovic.s: Časlav Klonimirović was Prince of Serbia in the 10th century and the last ruler of the Vlastimirović dynasty. Returning from Bulgaria in the late 920s, he restored the Serbian principality with Byzantine support after the Bulgarian conquest, ruling over much of the central…

constantine-dadeshkeliani.s: Constantine Dadeshkeliani was the last ruling prince of Svaneti in the Georgian Caucasus. Resisting the Russian authorities' plans to remove him, in 1857 he stabbed to death Prince Alexander Gagarin, the governor of Kutaisi, during a meeting.

cyril-of-turov.s: Cyril of Turov was bishop of Turov in the Pripyat marshes and one of the finest writers of early Rus'. His sermons for church feasts, prayers and parables, written in a rich rhetorical style modelled on Byzantine preaching, were copied widely.

canada-east.s: Canada East was the eastern, mainly French-speaking part of the Province of Canada from 1841 to 1867, corresponding to the former Lower Canada. Under the Act of Union it had the same number of seats in the assembly as Canada West, although at first it had the larger population.

canadian-american-reciprocity-treaty.s: The Canadian–American Reciprocity Treaty, also called the Elgin–Marcy Treaty, was signed in 1854 between Britain, on behalf of its North American colonies, and the United States. It removed duties on natural products such as grain, timber and fish and opened fisheries and…

continental-congress.s: The Continental Congress was the assembly of delegates from the Thirteen Colonies that directed American resistance to Britain and then governed the United States. The First Continental Congress met at Philadelphia in 1774; the Second, from 1775, created the Continental Army,…

constitutional-act-1791.s: The Constitutional Act of 1791 was a British law that divided the Province of Quebec into Upper Canada, mainly English-speaking, and Lower Canada, mainly French-speaking. Each province received an elected legislative assembly alongside an appointed council and governor, and…

charles-grant-1st-baron-glenelg.s: Charles Grant, 1st Baron Glenelg, was a Scottish politician who served as Secretary of State for War and the Colonies from 1835 to 1839. Influenced by humanitarian critics of colonial violence, he ordered the abandonment of the Province of Queen Adelaide in southern Africa in…

caracas.s: Caracas is the capital and largest city of Venezuela, in a mountain valley near the Caribbean coast. Founded by Diego de Losada in 1567 as Santiago de León de Caracas, it became the seat of the province of Venezuela and in 1777 of the Captaincy General.

cumana.s: Cumaná is a city on the north-eastern coast of Venezuela, capital of Sucre state. Founded by the Spanish in the early 16th century, it is often called the oldest surviving European-founded city in mainland South America, and it was the capital of the province of New Andalusia,…

committee-of-safety-hawaii.s: The Committee of Safety was a group of 13 mostly American and European businessmen and lawyers in Honolulu who organised the overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom in January 1893. Led by Lorrin A.

cestius-gallus.s: Gaius Cestius Gallus was the Roman governor of Syria from about 63 to 67 CE. In 66 he marched on Jerusalem to crush the Jewish revolt but withdrew, and his army was ambushed with heavy losses at Beth Horon.

cayuse-war.s: The Cayuse War was a conflict from 1847 to 1855 between the Cayuse people and American settlers in the Oregon Country. It was set off by the Whitman massacre of November 1847, when Cayuse men killed the missionaries Marcus and Narcissa Whitman and others after a measles…

champoeg.s: Champoeg was a settlement on the Willamette River in present-day Oregon, United States, where settlers met on 2 May 1843 and voted narrowly to form a provisional government, by tradition 52 votes to 50. It was the first American-style government on the Pacific coast.

curicaueri.s: Curicaueri was the fire and sun god of the Purépecha of western Mexico, patron of the ruling Uacúsecha lineage and of the Purépecha state. Priests kept fires burning in his honour on temple platforms, and war was waged to supply him with captives and firewood.

chimborazo.s: Chimborazo is an inactive stratovolcano in the Andes of central Ecuador, rising to 6,263 metres. Because of the Earth's equatorial bulge, its summit is the point on the surface farthest from the planet's centre.

cinekoy-inscription.s: The Çineköy inscription is a bilingual text in Luwian hieroglyphs and Phoenician carved on the base of a statue of the storm god found in 1997 at Çineköy, south of Adana in Turkey. Dating to the late 8th century BCE, it was set up by Warika (Awariku), king of Hiyawa, and…

chakradhar-singh.s: Chakradhar Singh was the Raja of Raigarh, a princely state in what is now Chhattisgarh, India, from 1924. A musician and dancer himself, he gathered leading Kathak dancers, singers and instrumentalists at his court and compiled treatises on dance and rhythm, giving rise to the…

cebu.s: Cebu is a long, narrow island in the central Visayas of the Philippines. Its east-coast port, now Cebu City, was the centre of a trading polity known as Sugbu when Ferdinand Magellan arrived in 1521 and baptised its ruler Humabon.

chulalongkorn.s: Chulalongkorn, King Rama V of Siam, reigned from 1868 to 1910. He abolished slavery and forced labour in stages, created ministries, a centralised provincial administration, railways and modern schools, and sent princes to study in Europe.

callejon-de-huaylas.s: The Callejón de Huaylas is the valley of the upper Santa River in the Ancash region of northern Peru, running between the snow-capped Cordillera Blanca and the Cordillera Negra. It was a heartland of the Recuay culture in the first centuries CE and lies close to Chavín de…

council-of-assiniboia.s: The Council of Assiniboia was the appointed governing body of the District of Assiniboia, the Red River Settlement in present-day Manitoba, from 1835 to 1870. Chosen by the Hudson's Bay Company and presided over by the governor of Assiniboia, it made laws, organised courts and…

caspe.s: Caspe is a town in the province of Zaragoza in Aragon, north-eastern Spain, near the Ebro River. It is best known for the Compromise of Caspe of 1412, which chose Ferdinand of Antequera as king of the Crown of Aragon.

confederacion-nacional-del-trabajo.s: The Confederación Nacional del Trabajo (CNT) is a Spanish anarcho-syndicalist trade union federation founded in Barcelona in 1910. By the 1930s it had well over a million members, and after the military rising of July 1936 its militias and collectives drove a social revolution…

courland-pocket.s: The Courland Pocket was the area of western Latvia where German Army Group North, later renamed Army Group Courland, was cut off by the Red Army from October 1944. Repeated Soviet offensives failed to destroy it, and around 200,000 German troops held out until the general…

chaco-war.s: The Chaco War was fought between Bolivia and Paraguay from 1932 to 1935 over the northern Gran Chaco, a region believed to hold oil. Paraguay, under José Félix Estigarribia, won most of the battles, and some 90,000 soldiers died on both sides, many from thirst and disease.

carlos-prio-socarras.s: Carlos Prío Socarrás was a Cuban politician of the Auténtico Party who was elected president in 1948. His government created the National Bank of Cuba but was widely seen as corrupt and plagued by political gang violence.

constitution-of-guaimaro.s: The Constitution of Guáimaro was adopted on 10 April 1869 by an assembly of Cuban rebels in the town of Guáimaro, in Camagüey, during the Ten Years' War. It created the Republic of Cuba in Arms, with a House of Representatives that elected Carlos Manuel de Céspedes president…

cuban-revolutionary-party.s: The Cuban Revolutionary Party was founded in 1892 by José Martí among Cuban and Puerto Rican exiles in the United States to prepare and finance a war for the independence of Cuba and Puerto Rico. It organised the uprising of February 1895 and represented the rebels abroad.

cosimo-de-medici.s: Cosimo de' Medici, called the Elder, was a Florentine banker who controlled the Republic of Florence from 1434 until his death without holding formal power for long. Head of the Medici Bank, then the largest in Europe, he governed through allies and manipulated councils and…

charlemagne-peralte.s: Charlemagne Péralte was a Haitian nationalist who led the Caco rebellion against the United States occupation of Haiti. A former army officer from Hinche, he raised guerrilla forces in 1918 against forced road labour (the corvée) and foreign rule.

constitution-of-latvia.s: The Constitution of Latvia, the Satversme, was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 15 February 1922 and came into force in November 1922. It established a parliamentary republic with a single-chamber Saeima and a president elected by parliament.

cape-palmas.s: Cape Palmas is a headland at the south-eastern end of Liberia, near the border with Côte d'Ivoire, where the coast of West Africa turns east into the Gulf of Guinea. In 1834 the Maryland State Colonization Society founded a settlement there, which became the independent…

california.s: California is a state on the Pacific coast of the United States and the country's most populous. Colonised by Spain from 1769 with missions and presidios as Alta California, it passed to Mexico in 1821 and was ceded to the United States after the Mexican–American War in 1848.

colon-free-zone.s: The Colón Free Zone is a duty-free trading zone beside the city of Colón, at the Caribbean entrance of the Panama Canal, created by law in 1948. Companies import goods there without customs duties and re-export them, mainly to Latin America and the Caribbean.

carlos-antonio-lopez.s: Carlos Antonio López was the ruler of Paraguay from 1841 until his death in 1862, first as consul and from 1844 as president. Ending the isolation imposed by José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia, he opened the country to trade, hired foreign engineers and built an ironworks, a…

callao.s: Callao is the chief port of Peru, on the Pacific coast immediately west of Lima. Founded by the Spanish in 1537, it was the main port of the Viceroyalty of Peru, from which silver was shipped to Panama, and it was rebuilt after a tsunami destroyed it in 1746.

calico-jack.s: Calico Jack, John Rackham, was an English pirate active in the Bahamas and Cuba from 1718 to 1720, late in the Golden Age of Piracy. He served as quartermaster to Charles Vane before replacing him as captain, and later sailed with the women pirates Anne Bonny and Mary Read.

charles-vane.s: Charles Vane was an English pirate who operated from Nassau in the Bahamas between 1716 and 1719. He refused the royal pardon brought by Governor Woodes Rogers in 1718, escaped from Nassau harbour by sending a fireship against Rogers's ships, and continued raiding.

catamarca-province.s: Catamarca is a province in north-western Argentina, with its capital at San Fernando del Valle de Catamarca, founded in 1683. Andean ranges and dry valleys cover much of it, and it was home to Diaguita peoples who resisted Spanish rule in the Calchaquí Wars.

calabria.s: Calabria is a region of southern Italy forming the 'toe' of the Italian peninsula, with Catanzaro as its capital. In antiquity its coasts held Greek colonies such as Rhegion, Croton and Locri.

ciutadella-de-roses.s: The Ciutadella de Roses is a fortified enclosure in Roses, Catalonia, built by the Spanish crown in the 16th century. Inside its walls excavations have uncovered the Greek colony of Rhode, a Roman settlement and the medieval monastery of Santa Maria.

cacapava-do-sul.s: Caçapava do Sul is a town in the centre of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. During the Ragamuffin War it served as one of the capitals of the Riograndense Republic, between Piratini and Alegrete, in the years around 1839 and 1840.

carausius.s: Carausius was a Roman military commander of Menapian origin who was given command of the Channel fleet against Frankish and Saxon pirates around 285. Accused of keeping captured plunder, he declared himself emperor in 286 and ruled Britain and part of northern Gaul until he…

cloaca-maxima.s: The Cloaca Maxima ('Greatest Sewer') is one of the oldest sewer systems in the world, built in ancient Rome to drain the marshy valley of the Forum into the Tiber. Tradition attributes it to the Etruscan kings of the 6th century BCE; it began as an open channel and was later…

constantine-algeria.s: Constantine is a city in north-eastern Algeria, built on a rocky plateau cut by the gorge of the Rhumel River. As Cirta it was the capital of the Numidian kings, and after it was rebuilt by Constantine the Great in the 4th century it took his name.

church-of-the-society-of-jesus-quito.n: Church of the Society of Jesus, Quito
church-of-the-society-of-jesus-quito.s: The Church of the Society of Jesus, known as La Compañía, is a Jesuit church in the historic centre of Quito, Ecuador, built from 1605 to 1765. Its interior, covered with gilded carving, is one of the finest examples of Spanish American Baroque and of the work of the Quito…

cree.s: The Cree are one of the largest Indigenous peoples of Canada, speaking Algonquian languages, with lands stretching from Quebec and the Hudson Bay lowlands to the northern plains. They were key partners of the Hudson's Bay Company in the fur trade, and the Plains Cree joined…

chikugo-province.s: Chikugo Province was an old province of Japan in northern Kyushu, corresponding to the southern part of modern Fukuoka Prefecture. Its plain along the Chikugo river was contested by the Otomo, Ryuzoji and Shimazu in the 16th century.

chikuzen-province.s: Chikuzen Province was an old province of Japan in northern Kyushu, covering the north-western part of modern Fukuoka Prefecture. Its port of Hakata was for centuries Japan's main gateway for trade with China and Korea.

claudia-gens.s: The Claudia gens was one of the great patrician families of ancient Rome, said to descend from the Sabine Attus Clausus, who settled in Rome around 504 BCE. Its members, proud and harsh in Roman tradition, included Appius Claudius Caecus, builder of the Via Appia.

cures.s: Cures was an ancient town of the Sabines north-east of Rome, near modern Fara in Sabina. Roman legend made it the home of the Sabine king Titus Tatius and of Numa Pompilius, Rome's second king.

chindwin-river.s: The Chindwin is a river of Myanmar and the largest tributary of the Irrawaddy, which it joins near Pakokku. It flows south for about 1,200 kilometres from the hills near the Indian border, and its valley has long been a route between Burma and Manipur.

chol-people.s: The Ch'ol are a Maya people whose language belongs to the Cholan branch of the Mayan family; today most live in northern Chiapas, Mexico. In the colonial period the Lacandon Ch'ol and the Manche Ch'ol of the southern lowland forests resisted Spanish rule until the late 17th…

chlodio.s: Chlodio was a king of the Salian Franks in the first half of the 5th century, mentioned by Gregory of Tours. Around the 440s he advanced into Roman territory, took Cambrai and occupied the land as far as the Somme, despite a defeat by the Roman general Aetius at Vicus Helena.

campine.s: The Campine, or Kempen, is a region of sandy heathland and pine forest in north-eastern Belgium and the southern Netherlands, roughly between the Scheldt, the Meuse and the Demer. In late Roman times it was part of Toxandria, where the Emperor Julian allowed the Salian Franks…

choe-regime.s: The Choe regime was the line of four military dictators of the Choe family who ruled Goryeo Korea from 1196 to 1258 while the kings remained figureheads. Founded by Choe Chung-heon, it governed through its own household agencies and private troops, including the Sambyeolcho.

caraceni.s: The Caraceni were the northernmost of the Samnite peoples of ancient Italy, living in the upper Sangro valley in modern Abruzzo and Molise, with their chief town probably at Aufidena. They formed one of the four peoples of the Samnite confederation alongside the Pentri,…

caudini.s: The Caudini were one of the four Samnite peoples of ancient Italy, living around Caudium in the hills between Campania and Samnium, near modern Montesarchio. The nearby pass of the Caudine Forks, where a Roman army surrendered in 321 BCE, takes its name from them.

coatzacoalcos-river.s: The Coatzacoalcos River rises in the mountains of Oaxaca and flows north through southern Veracruz, Mexico, to the Gulf of Mexico at the port city of Coatzacoalcos. Its floodplain was the heartland of the early Olmec civilisation, whose first great centre, San Lorenzo, stood…

charente.s: The Charente is a river of western France, about 380 kilometres long, which rises in the Limousin and flows past Angoulême, Cognac and Saintes to the Atlantic near Rochefort. In antiquity its valley was the land of the Santones, and in the Middle Ages it formed the heart of…

charente-maritime.s: Charente-Maritime is a department of western France on the Atlantic coast, in the region of Nouvelle-Aquitaine, with its prefecture at La Rochelle. It covers the historic province of Aunis and most of Saintonge, together with the islands of Ré and Oléron.

chertomlyk.s: Chertomlyk is a royal Scythian burial mound of the 4th century BCE near Nikopol in southern Ukraine, about 20 metres high. Excavated by Ivan Zabelin in 1862–1863, it held the burials of a king, his attendants and horses, together with a gilded silver amphora decorated with…

chabrias.s: Chabrias was an Athenian general of the 4th century BCE and a skilled commander of mercenaries and fleets. In 376 BCE his victory over the Spartan fleet off Naxos restored Athenian sea power and helped build the Second Athenian League.

cohen-plan.s: The Cohen Plan was a forged document, presented as a communist plan to seize power in Brazil, that the government of Getúlio Vargas made public in September 1937. Written by the Integralist officer Olímpio Mourão Filho, it was used to justify a state of war and the coup of 10…

constitutionalist-revolution.s: The Constitutionalist Revolution was an armed uprising of the state of São Paulo against the provisional government of Getúlio Vargas, fought from July to October 1932. The rebels demanded elections and a new constitution after Vargas had seized power in 1930 and appointed…

carlota-of-mexico.s: Carlota of Mexico, born Princess Charlotte of Belgium, was the daughter of Leopold I of Belgium and the wife of Maximilian, with whom she reigned as empress of Mexico from 1864 to 1867. In 1866 she travelled to Europe to seek help for the failing empire from Napoleon III and…

chapultepec-castle.s: Chapultepec Castle stands on a hill in Chapultepec Park in Mexico City. Begun in 1785 as a summer residence for the viceroys of New Spain, it later housed the military academy, whose young cadets died defending it against American troops in 1847.

castillejo-de-monteagudo.s: The Castillejo de Monteagudo is a ruined fortified palace near Murcia in south-eastern Spain, built in the mid-12th century for Muhammad ibn Mardanish, ruler of Murcia. It was a rectangular building with towers, set around a courtyard garden with pools, and stood at the centre…

cowkeeper.s: Cowkeeper, or Ahaya, was a Creek leader who led a group of Oconee people to the Alachua prairie in Florida around 1750. His town of Cuscowilla became the centre of the people who became known as the Seminole.

cattaraugus-reservation.s: The Cattaraugus Reservation is a territory of the Seneca Nation of Indians along Cattaraugus Creek, near Lake Erie in western New York. It was one of the lands kept by the Seneca after the Treaty of Big Tree in 1797.

cornplanter.s: Cornplanter was a Seneca war chief who fought on the British side in the American War of Independence and later sought peace with the United States. He took part in the treaties of the 1780s and 1790s and was granted land in Pennsylvania, where his descendants lived until the…

chaturvarga-chintamani.s: The Chaturvarga Chintamani is a vast Sanskrit digest of Hindu religious law and ritual compiled in the 13th century by Hemadri, minister of the Seuna Yadava kings. It deals with vows, gifts, pilgrimage, rites for the dead and other observances.

chinese-communist-party.s: The Chinese Communist Party is the founding and ruling party of the People's Republic of China. It held its first congress in the French Concession of Shanghai in 1921 and, under Mao Zedong, won the civil war against the Nationalists in 1949.

charles-belgrave.s: Charles Belgrave was a British official who served as adviser to the rulers of Bahrain from 1926 to 1957. Working with Sheikh Hamad ibn Isa Al Khalifa, he built up a modern administration, including courts, police, customs, municipal government and state schools, and…

cleisthenes.s: Cleisthenes was an Athenian statesman of the Alcmaeonid family, regarded as the founder of Athenian democracy. After the fall of the tyrant Hippias, he reorganised the citizen body in 508–507 BCE into ten new tribes based on local demes, broke the power of the old aristocratic…

cales.s: Cales was an ancient city of northern Campania, Italy, at modern Calvi Risorta. Originally an Ausonian town, it was captured by Rome, which founded a Latin colony there in 334 BCE on land taken from the Sidicini and Aurunci.

chaul.s: Chaul is a former port town on the Konkan coast in Raigad district, Maharashtra, India, south of Mumbai. An important harbour for Arab and Persian trade from early medieval times, it was the site of a sea battle in 1508 in which an Egyptian and Gujarati fleet defeated the…

caerleon.s: Caerleon is a town on the River Usk near Newport in south Wales. Around 75 CE the Romans built the legionary fortress of Isca Augusta there as the base of the Second Legion Augusta, whose amphitheatre, baths and barracks survive.

caerwent.s: Caerwent is a village in Monmouthshire, south-east Wales, on the site of Venta Silurum, the Roman town that served as the capital of the Silures. Its stone town walls are among the best preserved in Roman Britain, and an inscription there records the council of the civitas of…

chechens.s: The Chechens are a North Caucasian people of the Nakh group, living mainly in Chechnya in the Russian Federation. Largely Muslim since the 16th to 18th centuries, they resisted Russian conquest in the Caucasian War, notably under Imam Shamil.

candi-jago.s: Candi Jago is a 13th-century Hindu-Buddhist temple near Malang in East Java, built as the memorial shrine of King Wisnuwardhana of Singhasari, who died in 1268. Its terraced structure is covered with narrative reliefs, including scenes from the Kunjarakarna and the…

candi-singhasari.s: Candi Singhasari is a Hindu-Buddhist temple at Singosari near Malang in East Java, built around 1300 as a memorial to Kertanegara, the last king of Singhasari, who was killed in 1292. Dedicated mainly to Shiva, it is known for its unfinished carvings, which show how Javanese…

cerasus.s: Cerasus was an ancient Greek city on the southern Black Sea coast of Anatolia, founded as a colony of Sinope; its site is usually placed at or near modern Giresun in Turkey. Classical writers connected the city's name with the cherry (Greek kerasos), and tradition held that…

collectivity-of-saint-martin.s: The Collectivity of Saint Martin is the French northern part of the Caribbean island of Saint Martin, whose southern part is the Dutch Sint Maarten. The division of the island dates from the Treaty of Concordia of 1648.

cyclades.s: The Cyclades are a group of about 220 islands in the southern Aegean Sea, so called because they form a rough circle around the sacred island of Delos. They gave their name to the Early Bronze Age Cycladic culture, known for its marble figurines, and in later Greek history…

chao-mom-kham-le.s: Chao Mom Kham Le, known in Chinese as Dao Shixun, was the last hereditary ruler (chao phaendin) of the Tai Lue kingdom of Sipsong Panna in southern Yunnan. He succeeded as a young man in the 1940s, and after the Communist victory in China the old monarchy was replaced in 1953…

constantin-caratheodory.s: Constantin Carathéodory (1873–1950) was a Greek mathematician who spent most of his career in Germany. He made major contributions to the calculus of variations, measure theory and the theory of functions, and gave an axiomatic formulation of thermodynamics.

cherrapunji.s: Cherrapunji, also called Sohra, is a town on the southern edge of the Khasi Hills in Meghalaya, north-east India, overlooking the plains of Bangladesh. Monsoon winds rising against the hills give it one of the highest rainfalls on Earth, and it holds world records for rainfall…

chongzhen-emperor.s: The Chongzhen Emperor (1611–1644) was the last emperor of the Ming dynasty, reigning from 1627. Inheriting an empire beset by famine, peasant rebellions and Manchu invasions, he executed or dismissed many ministers and generals, including the commander Yuan Chonghuan.

chuuk-lagoon.s: Chuuk Lagoon, formerly Truk, is a large lagoon enclosed by a coral reef in the Caroline Islands, now part of the Federated States of Micronesia. Under Japanese rule it became the main forward base of the Imperial Japanese Navy's Combined Fleet in the Pacific.

cho-man-sik.s: Cho Man-sik (1883–1950) was a Korean Christian nationalist from Pyongyang, known for his non-violent resistance to Japanese rule and his campaign in the 1920s to buy Korean-made goods. After the Japanese surrender in 1945 he led the people's committee of South Pyongan under…

castillo-de-san-marcos.s: The Castillo de San Marcos is a Spanish masonry fort at St. Augustine, Florida, built between 1672 and 1695 from coquina, a local shell stone.

cape-juby.s: Cape Juby is a headland on the Atlantic coast of southern Morocco, opposite the Canary Islands, beside the town of Tarfaya. Under the Franco-Spanish agreements of 1912 the surrounding area became the southern zone of the Spanish protectorate in Morocco, administered from the…

caparra.s: Caparra was the first Spanish settlement in Puerto Rico, founded in 1508 by Juan Ponce de León a few kilometres inland from San Juan Bay. It served as the seat of government in the first years of the conquest, but its marshy, unhealthy site and distance from the harbour led…

castillo-san-felipe-del-morro.s: Castillo San Felipe del Morro is a Spanish citadel on the headland guarding the entrance to San Juan Bay in Puerto Rico. Begun in 1539 and expanded over two and a half centuries into a massive stone fortress, it withstood English and Dutch attacks, though the Earl of…

castillo-san-cristobal.s: Castillo San Cristóbal is a Spanish fortress in Old San Juan, Puerto Rico, built mainly between 1634 and 1783 to defend the city against attack by land. Covering some eleven hectares, it was the largest fortification built by Spain in the Americas.

chongqing.s: Chongqing is a city at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers in south-western China, made a municipality directly under the central government in 1997. In ancient times it was a centre of the State of Ba.

cao-shu-zhenduo.s: Cao Shu Zhenduo was a son of King Wen of Zhou and younger brother of King Wu, who after the Zhou conquest of Shang in the eleventh century BCE enfeoffed him at Taoqiu, in south-western Shandong. He became the founder of the ruling house of the State of Cao, which survived…

cartago-costa-rica.s: Cartago is a city in the central valley of Costa Rica, founded in 1563 by Juan Vázquez de Coronado. It was the colonial capital until 1823, when the capital moved to San José after a brief civil war between the towns.

church-of-jesus-christ-of-latter-day-sai.n: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
church-of-jesus-christ-of-latter-day-sai.s: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is the largest church of the Latter Day Saint movement, founded by Joseph Smith in New York in 1830. Persecuted in Missouri and Illinois, where Smith was killed in 1844, its members followed Brigham Young to the Salt Lake Valley…

comayagua.s: Comayagua is a city in central Honduras, founded in 1537 by the Spanish. As the seat of the colonial governors and bishops it was the capital of Honduras, and after independence it alternated with its rival Tegucigalpa as the seat of government until 1880, when the capital…

ceara.s: Ceará is a state in north-eastern Brazil, on the Atlantic coast, with its capital at Fortaleza. Settled slowly by the Portuguese from the seventeenth century, its dry interior became cattle country, and it was long subordinate to Maranhão or Pernambuco.

confucius.s: Confucius (Kong Qiu, Kongzi) was a teacher and minor official of the State of Lu whose sayings, collected by his disciples in the Analects, became the basis of Confucianism. He taught that good government rests on ritual propriety, benevolence and the moral example of the…

charles-warren.s: Sir Charles Warren was a British army officer and archaeologist. He surveyed Jerusalem in the 1860s, and in 1884–1885 led an expedition that ended the Boer republics of Stellaland and Goshen and secured British Bechuanaland.

cinco-villas.s: Cinco Villas is a comarca in the north-west of the province of Zaragoza in Aragon, Spain, named after five towns raised to the rank of villa by Philip V in the early 18th century. In antiquity the area was home to the Suessetani, and it contains Roman remains such as the town…

clades-lolliana.s: The clades Lolliana was a Roman defeat in 16 BCE, when the Sugambri, Usipetes and Tencteri crossed the Rhine and routed the legate Marcus Lollius, capturing the eagle of the Fifth Legion. Though limited in scale, the disgrace brought Augustus to Gaul and led to the campaigns…

chaamba.s: The Chaamba are an Arabic-speaking nomadic tribal confederation of the northern Algerian Sahara, centred on the region of Ouargla, Metlili and El Golea. They herded camels, traded and controlled caravan routes, and dealt with the oasis towns of the region.

cleisobora.s: Cleisobora was a city of the Surasena people of northern India mentioned by Greek and Roman writers drawing on the envoy Megasthenes, who visited India around 300 BCE. Arrian names it with Methora (Mathura) as a city where the people honoured Herakles, usually taken to mean…

chesapeake-bay.s: Chesapeake Bay is the largest estuary in the United States, extending about 300 kilometres from the mouth of the Susquehanna River in Maryland to the Atlantic in Virginia. Its shores were home to Algonquian peoples such as the Powhatan and to the Susquehannock, and the English…

crati.s: The Crati, the ancient Crathis, is the longest river of Calabria in southern Italy, flowing about 80 kilometres from the Sila mountains past Cosenza to the Gulf of Taranto. The Greek colony of Sybaris stood on the coastal plain near its mouth.

chepni.s: The Chepni are a Turkic tribe of the Oghuz family who settled in the Black Sea region of north-eastern Anatolia in the 13th and 14th centuries. They raided and pressed on the Empire of Trebizond and served local Turkmen beyliks of the Pontic hinterland.

cheorwon.s: Cheorwon is a county in the central highlands of the Korean peninsula, divided by the Demilitarised Zone between South Korea's Gangwon province and North Korea. In 905 Gung Ye moved the capital of his kingdom, later named Taebong, there from Songak, and remains of his capital…

calatayud.s: Calatayud is a town on the Jalón river in the province of Zaragoza, Aragon, Spain. It grew from the Muslim fortress of Qal'at Ayyub, founded in the 8th century near the ruins of Roman Bilbilis, birthplace of the poet Martial.

crevillent.s: Crevillent is a town at the foot of the Sierra de Crevillent in the province of Alicante, Valencian Community, Spain. After Murcia came under Castilian overlordship in the 1240s, it remained an autonomous Muslim lordship under the Banu Hudayr family until about 1318, when it…

cantar-de-mio-cid.s: The Cantar de mio Cid (Poem of the Cid) is the oldest surviving epic poem in Castilian Spanish, telling of the exile and triumphs of Rodrigo Díaz, El Cid. Composed around 1200, it survives in a single 14th-century manuscript copied from a text signed by a certain Per Abbat.

ciudad-perdida.s: Ciudad Perdida ('Lost City'), known to the Indigenous peoples as Teyuna, is an archaeological site in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, northern Colombia. Founded around 800 CE, it was a major Tairona town with about 170 stone terraces linked by stairways and paved paths.

charles-james-napier.s: Sir Charles James Napier (1782–1853) was a British general who conquered Sindh in 1843. After defeating the Talpur mirs at Miani and Dubba near Hyderabad, he annexed the province and governed it until 1847, and he later served as commander-in-chief in India.

chaiya.s: Chaiya is a town and district in Surat Thani province in southern Thailand, near the Bay of Bandon. An important centre in the era of Srivijaya, it is known for the temple of Wat Phra Borommathat Chaiya and for Buddhist sculptures and inscriptions, among them an inscription of…

cancho-roano.s: Cancho Roano is an archaeological site near Zalamea de la Serena in the province of Badajoz, Extremadura, western Spain. Its building, dating from about the 6th to the late 5th century BCE, is interpreted as a palace-sanctuary of the late Tartessian world and was deliberately…

ciaruteun-inscription.s: The Ciaruteun inscription is a 5th-century stone inscription found in the Ciaruteun stream near Bogor in West Java, Indonesia. Written in Sanskrit in a Pallava script, it is carved with a pair of footprints that it compares to those of Vishnu and attributes to King Purnawarman…

cleitus-of-illyria.s: Cleitus was an Illyrian king of the 4th century BCE, son of Bardylis, whose realm lay on the north-western borders of Macedon. In 335 BCE he rose against Alexander the Great and, with the Taulantian king Glaukias, held the fortress of Pelion.

cuicuilco.s: Cuicuilco is an archaeological site in the south of Mexico City, the remains of one of the earliest large centres of the Valley of Mexico. From about 800 BCE it grew into a town with a large circular platform-pyramid and was the main rival of early Teotihuacan.

chuuk.s: Chuuk is a state of the Federated States of Micronesia, centred on Chuuk Lagoon in the Caroline Islands. As Truk it was Japan's main naval base in the central Pacific during the Second World War, and American air raids in February 1944 sank dozens of ships there.

curtis-island.s: Curtis Island is a large island off the coast of central Queensland, Australia, near the port of Gladstone. In the 1960s the Australian government proposed resettling the whole population of Nauru there, as phosphate mining was making their island uninhabitable, but the…

cacamatzin.s: Cacamatzin was the ruler of Texcoco from 1516 to 1520, a son of Nezahualpilli and nephew of the Mexica ruler Moctezuma II. Chosen with Mexica backing over his brother Ixtlilxochitl II, he was seized by Hernán Cortés in 1520 after plotting resistance to the Spanish.

carnatic-sultanate.s: The Carnatic Sultanate was a state in south-eastern India ruled by the Nawabs of the Carnatic, or of Arcot, from about 1692 to 1855. First Mughal governors, the nawabs became independent rulers but were drawn into the Carnatic Wars between Britain and France and fell under…

ciudad-bolivar.s: Ciudad Bolívar is the capital of Bolívar state in south-eastern Venezuela, on the south bank of the Orinoco at its narrowest point. Founded in 1764 as Angostura, it became Simón Bolívar's base in the war of independence: the Congress of Angostura met there in 1819, and the…

correo-del-orinoco.s: The Correo del Orinoco was a newspaper published at Angostura, now Ciudad Bolívar, from 1818 to 1822 by the patriot government of Simón Bolívar. It promoted the cause of independence, printed official decrees and news of the war, and answered royalist propaganda.

chanthaburi.s: Chanthaburi is a city in south-eastern Thailand near the Cambodian border, long known for its gem trade and fruit orchards. After the fall of Ayutthaya in 1767, Taksin seized the town and used it as the base where he gathered troops and built a fleet before driving the Burmese…

chiavenna.s: Chiavenna is a town in Lombardy, northern Italy, where the routes over the Splügen and Maloja passes from Switzerland meet. Long a staging post on Alpine trade routes, it was conquered by the Three Leagues of the Grisons in 1512 and governed by them as a subject county until…

codex-bodley.s: The Codex Bodley is a pre-Hispanic Mixtec manuscript painted on a folded strip of deerskin, now in the Bodleian Library at Oxford. Read in horizontal bands, it records the genealogies, marriages and wars of the ruling families of Tilantongo and other Mixtec kingdoms of Oaxaca…

codex-zouche-nuttall.s: The Codex Zouche-Nuttall is a pre-Hispanic Mixtec manuscript painted on deerskin and folded like a screen, now in the British Museum. One side records the histories of several Mixtec centres, the other the life and conquests of the 11th-century ruler Eight Deer Jaguar Claw of…

cuacuauhpitzahuac.s: Cuacuauhpitzahuac was the first tlatoani of Tlatelolco, the twin city of Tenochtitlan in the Valley of Mexico, ruling from the 1370s to about 1418. A son of Tezozomoc, ruler of the Tepanec city of Azcapotzalco, he was installed under Tepanec protection, and Tlatelolco grew as…

chorni-klobuky.s: The Chorni Klobuky, 'Black Hats', were a union of Turkic nomad groups, including Torks, Berendei and Pechenegs, settled by the princes of Kiev along the Ros River south of the city in the 11th and 12th centuries. In return for land they served as frontier cavalry against the…

cakaudrove-province.s: Cakaudrove is a province of Fiji covering south-eastern Vanua Levu, Taveuni and nearby islands, traditionally ruled by the Tui Cakau from Somosomo. In the 19th century it was one of the leading powers of eastern Fiji, and in 1867 its chiefs joined Enele Maʻafu of Lau and the…

chalcis.s: Chalcis is the chief town of the Greek island of Euboea, on the narrow Euripus strait facing the mainland. In antiquity it was a major city that founded many colonies in Italy, Sicily and the northern Aegean.

camulodunum.s: Camulodunum, modern Colchester in Essex, was the chief centre of the Trinovantes and later of Cunobelinus, a vast oppidum protected by long earthwork dykes. After the Roman invasion of 43 CE it became the first capital of Roman Britain and a colony of veterans with a temple to…

chakla-roshnabad.s: Chakla Roshnabad was a large estate in the plains west of the Tripura hills, in the districts of Comilla, Noakhali and Sylhet in present-day Bangladesh. After the Mughals annexed these lowlands, the Manikya kings of Tripura kept them as zamindars, paying revenue first to the…

castle-bravo.s: Castle Bravo was the first American test of a deliverable dry-fuel hydrogen bomb, exploded at Bikini Atoll on 1 March 1954. Its yield of about 15 megatons, far more than predicted, made it the largest nuclear explosion ever carried out by the United States.

congress-of-micronesia.s: The Congress of Micronesia was the elected legislature of the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands, created in 1965 and first convened at Saipan. It became the forum in which Micronesian leaders negotiated their future political status with the United States.

chahar-mongols.s: The Chahar are a Mongol people of Inner Mongolia. In the 16th century they formed one of the six tumens of Dayan Khan's restored Mongol realm and were the personal following of the Great Khan.

chahar-province.s: Chahar Province was a province of the Republic of China, created in 1928 from a special district north-west of Beijing, with its capital at Kalgan (Zhangjiakou). Named after the Chahar Mongols, it combined Mongol grazing lands with Chinese farming districts.

caupo.s: Caupo was a chieftain of the Livonians at Turaida on the Gauja river in present-day Latvia. He accepted Christianity early, travelled to Rome around 1203 to meet Pope Innocent III and became a firm ally of Bishop Albert of Riga and the German crusaders, even against his own…

culchas.s: Culchas was a ruler in southern Spain during and after the Second Punic War. Livy records that in 206 BCE he controlled 28 towns and supplied troops to Scipio against the Carthaginians.

caicos-islands.s: The Caicos Islands are the larger of the two island groups of the Turks and Caicos Islands, a British overseas territory south-east of the Bahamas. They include Providenciales, North, Middle, East, South and West Caicos.

cockburn-town.s: Cockburn Town is the capital of the Turks and Caicos Islands, on the island of Grand Turk. It grew from the settlement of Bermudian salt rakers who worked the salt ponds of Grand Turk from the late 17th century, and salt remained the islands' chief export for two centuries.

castor-and-pollux.s: Castor and Pollux, the Dioscuri, were twin heroes and gods of Greek and Roman religion, sons of Leda and, in most accounts, of Zeus. They were patrons of horsemen and protectors of sailors.

circe.s: Circe is an enchantress of Greek mythology, a daughter of the sun god Helios, who lived on the island of Aeaea. In Homer's Odyssey she turns Odysseus' companions into pigs, but Odysseus, protected by a herb from Hermes, compels her to restore them and stays with her for a year.

chakhundorj.s: Chakhundorj was Tüsheet Khan, ruler of central Khalkha Mongolia, from 1655 to 1699, and the elder brother of Zanabazar. His war with the western Khalkha Zasagt Khan in 1687, in which the Zasagt Khan was killed, gave the Dzungar ruler Galdan a pretext to invade Khalkha in 1688.

carnegie-institution-for-science.s: The Carnegie Institution for Science is a research organisation founded in Washington in 1902 by the industrialist Andrew Carnegie, long known as the Carnegie Institution of Washington. From 1914 to 1958 it ran a major programme of Maya research, led by Sylvanus Morley and…

congo-ocean-railway.s: The Congo–Ocean Railway runs for about 500 kilometres from Brazzaville to the port of Pointe-Noire in the Republic of the Congo. It was built by French Equatorial Africa between 1921 and 1934 with forced labour recruited across the federation, including Ubangi-Shari and Chad.

county-limerick.s: County Limerick is a county in the province of Munster in western Ireland, lying south of the Shannon estuary around the city of Limerick. In the early Middle Ages its west was held by the Uí Fidgenti, while the Norse founded Limerick itself in the 10th century.

chernobyl-disaster.s: The Chernobyl disaster was the explosion and fire at reactor No. 4 of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant in the Ukrainian SSR on 26 April 1986, the worst accident in the history of nuclear power.

coutances.s: Coutances is a town in the Cotentin peninsula of Normandy, France. In Roman times, as Cosedia, it became the chief town of the Gallic Unelli, and it was renamed Constantia in late antiquity, a name that also gave the Cotentin its name.

cartagena-manifesto.s: The Cartagena Manifesto is a political statement written by Simón Bolívar in Cartagena de Indias in December 1812, after the fall of the First Republic of Venezuela. Bolívar blamed the defeat on federalism, weak government and leniency towards royalists, and called for a…

congress-of-tucuman.s: The Congress of Tucumán was the assembly of deputies from the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata that met in San Miguel de Tucumán from March 1816. On 9 July 1816 it declared independence from Spain, a date now celebrated as Argentina's Independence Day.

carlos-finlay.s: Carlos Finlay was a Cuban physician and epidemiologist who in 1881 proposed that yellow fever was transmitted by a mosquito, now known as Aedes aegypti. His theory was confirmed in 1900 by the United States Army commission led by Walter Reed during the American occupation of…

charles-de-thierry.s: Charles de Thierry was an adventurer of French émigré family who claimed to have bought land at Hokianga in New Zealand in 1820 and in 1835 announced his intention to make himself sovereign chief of the country. His claim alarmed the British Resident James Busby, who responded…

cato-the-younger.s: Cato the Younger (Marcus Porcius Cato) was a Roman senator and Stoic, great-grandson of Cato the Elder, famed for his rigid integrity and defence of the traditional Republic. He opposed Julius Caesar and sided with Pompey in the civil war.

chaac.s: Chaac is the Maya god of rain, lightning and storms, often shown with a long curling nose and an axe that strikes the clouds to bring rain. He was especially important in the dry Puuc region of Yucatán, where long-nosed masks traditionally identified with him cover the façades…

calagurris.s: Calagurris was a town of the Vascones on the Ebro in northern Spain, the site of modern Calahorra in La Rioja. It backed Sertorius in his war against the Roman Senate and fell to Pompey's forces in 72 BCE after a siege so harsh that the defenders were said to have eaten their…

cemenelum.s: Cemenelum was a Roman town on the hill of Cimiez above Nice, in south-eastern France, the capital of the province of Alpes Maritimae. It grew from a settlement of the Ligurian Vediantii and a military post.

carpow.s: Carpow is the site of a Roman legionary fortress on the south bank of the Tay near Abernethy in Perth and Kinross, Scotland. It was built around 208–211, during the campaigns of the emperor Septimius Severus against the Caledonians and Maeatae, and was garrisoned by…

castro-de-el-raso.s: The Castro de El Raso is an Iron Age hillfort at Candeleda in the province of Ávila, Spain, on the southern slopes of the Sierra de Gredos. Occupied by the Vettones from about the 4th century BCE until it was abandoned around the time of the Roman conquest in the 1st century…

colline-metallifere.s: The Colline Metallifere ('metal-bearing hills') are a range of hills in southern Tuscany, Italy, spanning the provinces of Grosseto, Siena, Pisa and Livorno. Their copper, iron, silver and lead ores were worked by the Etruscans and enriched cities such as Vetulonia and…

cuyo.s: Cuyo is a historical region of western Argentina at the foot of the Andes, made up of the provinces of Mendoza, San Juan and San Luis. Settled from Chile in the 1560s, it was governed from Santiago until 1776, when it was transferred to the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata.

caen.s: Caen is a city on the River Orne in Normandy, north-western France. It grew under William the Conqueror, who built its castle and, with his wife Matilda of Flanders, founded the Abbaye aux Hommes and the Abbaye aux Dames in the 1060s; it later housed the Exchequer of Normandy.

chandragiri.s: Chandragiri is a town near Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh, India, with a fort and palace complex on a rocky hill. It became a capital of the last Vijayanagara rulers of the Aravidu dynasty in the late 16th and 17th centuries, and in 1639 the grant of the site of Madras to the…

chalus.s: Châlus is a small town in the Haute-Vienne department of the Limousin, central France. While besieging its castle of Châlus-Chabrol, held for the viscount of Limoges, King Richard I of England was struck by a crossbow bolt on 26 March 1199 and died of the wound on 6 April.

charles-godefroy-de-la-tour-dauvergne.s: Charles-Godefroy de La Tour d'Auvergne was a French nobleman, Duke of Bouillon from 1730 and the last viscount of Turenne. Burdened by his family's debts, in 1738 he sold the viscounty of Turenne to Louis XV, ending its quasi-independent status and its tax privileges.

church-of-the-intercession-on-the-nerl.n: Church of the Intercession on the Nerl
church-of-the-intercession-on-the-nerl.s: The Church of the Intercession on the Nerl is a white-stone church near Bogolyubovo, outside Vladimir in Russia, built in 1165 under Andrei Bogolyubsky. Standing in a water meadow near where the Nerl joins the Klyazma, it is famed for its slender, harmonious form and carved…

cecina-river.s: The Cecina is a river of western Tuscany, Italy, about 80 km long, rising in the Colline Metallifere and flowing west to the Tyrrhenian Sea at the town of Cecina. Its valley, below the ridge of Volterra, has salt springs and formed the heart of the territory of the Etruscan…

crocifisso-del-tufo.s: The Crocifisso del Tufo is an Etruscan necropolis below the cliffs of Orvieto in Umbria, Italy, used mainly in the 6th and 5th centuries BCE. Its chamber tombs, built of tufa blocks, are laid out in a regular grid of streets, and many bear the names of their owners carved on…

caelius-vibenna.s: Caelius Vibenna (Etruscan Caile Vipinas) was an Etruscan warrior leader of the 6th century BCE from Vulci, who appears with his brother Aulus in Roman tradition and Etruscan art. The François Tomb shows him being freed from captivity by Macstrna, and the Romans held that the…

cape-cod.s: Cape Cod is a hook-shaped peninsula in south-eastern Massachusetts reaching about 100 kilometres into the Atlantic Ocean. It was home to Wampanoag and Nauset communities when the Pilgrims of the Mayflower anchored at its tip in November 1620 before settling at Plymouth.

cerro-baul.s: Cerro Baúl is a flat-topped mountain in the Moquegua valley of southern Peru, on whose summit the Wari Empire built a fortified colony around 600 CE. It faced settlements of the rival Tiwanaku state in the same valley and held palaces, temples and a large brewery for the…

cal-madow.s: Cal Madow is a mountain range in northern Somalia, running east to west near the Gulf of Aden coast, mainly in the Sanaag region and into Bari. Its highest point, Shimbiris, at about 2,400 metres, is the highest mountain in Somalia.

creevelea-friary.s: Creevelea Friary is a ruined Franciscan friary near Dromahair in County Leitrim, Ireland, founded in 1508 by Margaret O'Brien and her husband Eoghan O'Rourke, lord of West Breifne. It was one of the last Franciscan houses founded in Ireland before the Reformation.

chavundaraya.s: Chavundaraya was a minister and military commander of the Western Ganga kings Marasimha II and Rachamalla IV in the late 10th century. A devout Jain, he commissioned around 983 the giant statue of Bahubali, known as Gommateshwara, at Shravanabelagola.

chastana.s: Chastana was a Saka ruler of western India in the early 2nd century CE who founded the Kardamaka line of the Western Satraps, with his capital at Ujjain. Known from coins and inscriptions, he may first have governed as a Kushan subordinate.

changzi.s: Changzi is a county in south-eastern Shanxi, China, now part of the city of Changzhi. In 386 the Xianbei leader Murong Yong made it the capital of the Western Yan, one of the Sixteen Kingdoms.

caribbean-community.s: The Caribbean Community, CARICOM, is an organisation of Caribbean states and dependencies founded by the Treaty of Chaguaramas in 1973 to promote economic integration and cooperation in foreign policy, health and education. It succeeded the Caribbean Free Trade Association and…

chigu.s: Chigu, the 'Red Valley City', was the royal seat of the Wusun, a nomadic people of the Ili and Issyk-Kul region, as recorded in the Han dynasty histories. From it the Wusun ruler, the kunmo, governed a population the Han counted at some 630,000.

chaghaniyan.s: Chaghaniyan was a medieval principality in the valley of the Surkhan Darya, in present-day southern Uzbekistan, north of the Amu Darya. Ruled by local princes titled Chaghan Khudah, it was one of the lordships of Tokharistan under the Western Turks before the Arab conquests of…

crnojevic-noble-family.s: The Crnojević family ruled Zeta, the core of present-day Montenegro, in the fifteenth century. Rising after the decline of the Balšić lords, they led the highland clans between the Ottomans and Venice.

cetinje.s: Cetinje is a town in a high karst basin of southern Montenegro and the country's old royal capital. Ivan Crnojević moved his seat there in 1482 and founded its monastery, which became the residence of the prince-bishops who led Montenegro until 1852.

cetinje-octoechos.s: The Cetinje Octoechos, or Oktoih, is a book of Orthodox liturgical hymns printed in 1494 by the monk Makarije at the press of Đurađ Crnojević in Cetinje. It is the first book printed in Cyrillic among the South Slavs and one of the earliest Cyrillic printed books anywhere.

christopher-soames.s: Christopher Soames, Lord Soames, was a British Conservative politician and son-in-law of Winston Churchill. After serving as ambassador to France and as a European commissioner, he was appointed the last Governor of Southern Rhodesia in December 1979, overseeing the ceasefire…

cetshwayo.s: Cetshwayo kaMpande was king of the Zulu from 1872 to 1879. He won the succession by defeating his brother Mbuyazi at Ndondakusuka in 1856, rebuilt the regimental system and made Ulundi his capital.

cairo-geniza.s: The Cairo Geniza is a collection of some 400,000 manuscript fragments kept in the storeroom (geniza) of the Ben Ezra Synagogue in Fustat, Old Cairo, where worn writings bearing the name of God were laid aside rather than destroyed. Its letters, contracts and accounts, mostly…

carolingian-civil-war.s: The Carolingian civil war (840–843) was fought among the sons of Emperor Louis the Pious over the Frankish empire after his death in 840. Lothair I, who claimed the whole empire, was defeated at Fontenoy in 841 by his brothers Louis the German and Charles the Bald, who…

caesars-civil-war.s: Caesar's Civil War was fought from 49 to 45 BCE between Julius Caesar and the conservative faction of the Roman Senate led by Pompey. It began when Caesar crossed the Rubicon into Italy in January 49 BCE; his victories at Pharsalus (48), Thapsus (46) and Munda (45) left him…

chilean-war-of-independence.s: The Chilean War of Independence was the struggle of Chilean patriots against Spanish royalist rule, from the first national junta of 1810 to the capture of Chiloé in 1826. After royalist forces reconquered Chile in 1814, the Army of the Andes under José de San Martín and…

chinese-civil-war.s: The Chinese Civil War was fought between the Nationalist government of the Kuomintang and the Chinese Communist Party, in two phases from 1927 to 1937 and from 1945 to 1949, interrupted by the war against Japan. The Communists under Mao Zedong won and proclaimed the People's…

cleomenean-war.s: The Cleomenean War was fought from 229 to 222 BCE between Sparta under King Cleomenes III and the Achaean League. Cleomenes, who had carried out radical reforms at home, defeated the Achaeans repeatedly, prompting their leader Aratus to seek help from Antigonus III Doson of…

chola-chalukya-wars.s: The Chola–Chalukya wars were a long series of conflicts in the 11th and early 12th centuries between the Chola dynasty of the Tamil country and the Western Chalukyas of Kalyani in the Deccan. They fought chiefly over the fertile Raichur Doab and over influence in the Eastern…

corinthian-war.s: The Corinthian War was fought from 395 to 387 BCE between Sparta and an alliance of Thebes, Athens, Corinth and Argos, supported at first by Persia. Sparta won on land at Nemea and Coronea but lost its fleet at Cnidus (394 BCE); the war ended with the King's Peace of 387 BCE,…

cochinchina-campaign.s: The Cochinchina campaign was a war fought from 1858 to 1862 by France and Spain against the Nguyễn dynasty of Vietnam. Begun as a punitive expedition over the persecution of Catholic missionaries, it ended with the Treaty of Saigon (1862), by which Vietnam ceded three southern…

conquest-of-wales-by-edward-i.n: Conquest of Wales by Edward I
conquest-of-wales-by-edward-i.s: The conquest of Wales by Edward I was the series of English campaigns of 1277 and 1282–1283 that ended the independent Welsh principality ruled from Gwynedd. After Llywelyn ap Gruffudd was killed in December 1282 and his brother Dafydd captured, Edward annexed the…

castilian-civil-war.s: The Castilian Civil War was fought from 1351 to 1369 between King Peter of Castile and his half-brother Henry of Trastámara. It became part of the Anglo-French conflict, with England supporting Peter and France sending Bertrand du Guesclin to aid Henry; despite Peter's victory…

civil-wars-between-the-conquistadors-in-.n: Civil wars between the conquistadors in Peru
civil-wars-between-the-conquistadors-in-.s: The civil wars between the conquistadors in Peru were fought from 1537 to 1554 among the Spanish conquerors of the Inca Empire and against royal authority. Francisco Pizarro defeated Diego de Almagro at Las Salinas (1538), Almagro's followers killed Pizarro in 1541, and…

caucasus-campaign.s: The Caucasus campaign was the First World War theatre in which the Ottoman Empire fought Russia, and later Armenia, Azerbaijan and other states, in the Caucasus and eastern Anatolia from 1914 to 1918. After the Ottoman disaster at Sarikamish (1914–1915), Russia advanced as far…

crusade-of-varna.s: The Crusade of Varna was a campaign of 1443–1444 against the Ottoman Empire by Hungary, Poland, Wallachia and others, led by King Władysław III and John Hunyadi. After the successful 'Long Campaign' of 1443 and the Peace of Szeged, the crusaders renewed the war and were…

central-american-civil-war.s: The Central American Civil War was fought from 1826 to 1829 within the Federal Republic of Central America between conservatives, led by President Manuel José Arce, and liberals. The liberal forces of Francisco Morazán won, taking Guatemala City in 1829, and Morazán became…

caucasian-war.s: The Caucasian War was the Russian Empire's long conquest of the North Caucasus, from 1817 to 1864. Russia faced fierce resistance from the peoples of Chechnya and Dagestan, united under Imam Shamil until his surrender in 1859, and from the Circassians in the north-west, whose…

civil-war-era-in-norway.s: The civil war era in Norway was a period of intermittent wars between rival claimants to the Norwegian throne from 1130 to 1240. With no fixed succession law, any son of a king could claim the crown, and factions such as the Birkebeiner and Bagler fought for power.

croatian-ottoman-wars.s: The Croatian–Ottoman wars were a long series of conflicts between the Kingdom of Croatia and the Ottoman Empire from the fifteenth century to the end of the sixteenth. Ottoman raids and conquests, including the victory at Krbava Field in 1493, reduced Croatia to a narrow remnant.

cuban-revolution.s: The Cuban Revolution was the armed rising led by Fidel Castro and his 26th of July Movement against the dictatorship of Fulgencio Batista. It began with the attack on the Moncada Barracks in 1953, and from 1956 guerrillas fought from the Sierra Maestra.

catalan-civil-war.s: The Catalan Civil War was fought from 1462 to 1472 between King John II of Aragon and the Principality of Catalonia, whose institutions rejected his rule and offered the crown to several rival princes. The remença peasants supported the king.

chilean-civil-war-of-1829-1830.s: The Chilean Civil War of 1829–1830 was fought between the liberals, known as pipiolos, and the conservatives, known as pelucones, after disputed elections in 1829. The conservative army under Joaquín Prieto defeated the liberal forces under Ramón Freire at the Battle of Lircay…

cimbrian-war.s: The Cimbrian War was fought from 113 to 101 BCE between the Roman Republic and the migrating Cimbri and Teutones. The tribes inflicted several defeats on Roman armies, worst at Arausio in 105 BCE.

cambodian-vietnamese-war.s: The Cambodian–Vietnamese War was fought between Vietnam and the Khmer Rouge regime of Democratic Kampuchea, which had launched border raids. Vietnam invaded in December 1978, took Phnom Penh in January 1979 and installed the People's Republic of Kampuchea.

chickasaw-wars.s: The Chickasaw Wars were fought in the eighteenth century between the Chickasaw, allied with the British, and the French of Louisiana with their Choctaw allies in the lower Mississippi valley. French invasions of the Chickasaw homeland in northern Mississippi were defeated at…
